| `SvOptionsNodeTile` | `SvTitledTile` | Container for selectable options (`role="listbox"`). |
| `SvOptionNodeTile` | `SvTitledTile` | Individual selectable option (`role="option"`). |

### Chat Tiles

| Class | Extends | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `SvChatMessageTile` | `SvTextAreaFieldTile` | Chat bubble with HTML support, accessibility, and speech capability. |
| `SvChatInputTile` | `SvChatMessageTile` | Multiline chat input. |

### Resource Tiles

| Class | Extends | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `SvImageTile` | `SvTitledTile` | Image display with caption derived from node title. |
| `SvFontTile` | `SvTitledTile` | Font preview showing family, style, weight, and stretch. |

## Proposed Tiles

### Rich Text Tile

A tile whose value area supports formatted text (bold, italic, lists, headings) rather than plain text. Useful for notes, journal entries, descriptions, and any long-form content. Would need to bridge the node's value to a contentEditable region with structured markup.

### Media Tile

A standalone playback tile that embeds audio or video transport controls (play/pause, scrubbing, volume). The node would reference a sound or video resource; the tile provides the playback UI. Builds on the existing `SvWaSound` infrastructure for audio and could extend to video via standard HTML5 media elements.

The existing `SvVideoWellFieldTile` and `SvSceneViewWellFieldTile` handle drag-and-drop *input* of media files. This proposed tile is the complement: *playback* of media already associated with a node.

### Meter / Progress Tile

A tile that renders a numeric slot value as a visual meter, progress bar, or gauge. The slot's `minimum` and `maximum` annotations define the range -- the same annotations that already drive `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax`. Useful for hit points, loading progress, skill levels, and any bounded numeric value.

### Badge / Status Tile

A compact tile optimized for small status indicators -- an icon plus a short label, possibly color-coded by state. Useful for tags, status markers, notification counts, and online/offline indicators. Would pair well with the wrapping grid container for dense displays.

### Document Tile

A tile that composes a node's subnode tree into a rendered document. The subnodes represent the structural elements of a document -- headings, paragraphs, images, code blocks, lists -- each as an independent node with its own metadata. The document tile walks this subtree and renders the composed result inline as formatted HTML or markdown.

The structural editing happens in the normal tile container: subnodes appear as draggable tiles that can be reordered, added, or removed. The document tile provides the complementary view -- the same content rendered as a reader would see it. A node could support both views (structural and composed) via the user-switchable container mechanism described in [Tile Container Views](../Tile%20Container%20Views/), letting the user toggle between editing the structure and previewing the document.

Use cases include blog posts, reports, style guides, documentation pages, and any content where the author benefits from structural manipulation (drag a section to a new position, tag individual blocks with metadata, collapse sections) but the reader needs a coherent rendered document.

### Embed Tile

A tile that renders an iframe or sandboxed external content. The node provides a URL; the tile handles sizing, loading states, and security boundaries. Useful for embedding external widgets, previews, or third-party content within the node hierarchy.

## Design Considerations

- **Slot-driven rendering**: New tiles should derive their behavior from slot metadata wherever possible (type, annotations, description), keeping domain objects declarative rather than view-aware.
- **Tile class selection**: Nodes opt in via `setNodeTileClass(SvImageTile)` etc. The framework's existing view-discovery mechanism handles the rest.
- **Accessibility**: Each new tile needs appropriate ARIA roles and state, following the `SvNodeView_accessibility` pattern. For example, a meter tile would use `role="meter"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuenow`.
- **Composability with containers**: New tile types should work in any container -- a media tile in a list, an image tile in a wrapping grid, a badge tile in a spatial map.

<!-- Page: docs/Getting Started -->
Source: /docs/Getting%20Started/

# Getting Started

Setup, integration, directory conventions, build pipeline, and running your first Strvct application.

## Overview

Strvct is designed to be integrated directly into your application codebase as a **Git submodule**. It runs as a client-side single-page application in the browser and requires no compile-step template transforms, virtual DOM bundlers, or complex build toolchains.

### Quick Workflow Overview:
1. **Add Submodule:** Link Strvct as a git submodule in your repository.
2. **Declare Imports:** List application source files in `_imports.json`.
3. **Run Build:** Generate CAM catalog artifacts (`_index.json` and `_cam.json.zip`).
4. **Start Server:** Launch `CliWebServer.js` locally.
5. **Create Nodes:** Author annotated domain models inheriting from `SvStorableNode`.
6. **Debug:** Inspect live state and set breakpoints in Chrome DevTools or Cursor/VSCode.

---

## Prerequisites

Before starting, ensure you have the following installed:
- **Git** (with submodule support)
- **Node.js** (v18+ recommended)
- **Cursor / VSCode** (for Chrome DevTools debugging support)

---

## Adding Strvct to Your Project

From your project's root directory, add Strvct as a Git submodule:

```bash
git submodule add https://github.com/stevedekorte/strvct.net.git strvct
```

If deploying your application to GitHub Pages or static hosts that run Jekyll by default, create a `.nojekyll` file in your root folder:

```bash
touch .nojekyll
```

---

## Directory Structure & Conventions

A standard Strvct application uses the following directory layout:

```
your-project/
├── strvct/              # Framework submodule
├── app/                 # Application domain models & source code
│   ├── _imports.json    # Declares app source files
│   └── Character.js     # Your domain classes
├── resources/           # Binary assets (icons, images, sounds)
├── build/               # Generated CAM artifacts (git-ignored)
│   ├── _index.json      # Resource metadata catalog with SHA-256 hashes
│   └── _cam.json.zip    # Zip bundle of hashed assets
├── _imports.json        # Root imports file (links strvct + app)
├── index.html           # HTML entry point
└── .nojekyll            # Prevents GitHub Pages Jekyll processing
```

---

## Declaring Imports (`_imports.json`)

Strvct uses `_imports.json` files to discover source files and manage dependency order instead of standard ES module imports. Every folder containing JavaScript or CSS resources specifies an `_imports.json` array:

```json
[
    "_css.css",
    "strvct/_imports.json",
    "app/_imports.json"
]
```

### Import Rules:
- Paths are relative to the directory containing the `_imports.json` file.
- Direct file paths (e.g., `"Character.js"`, `"_css.css"`) are included in order.
- Nested `_imports.json` paths (e.g., `"app/_imports.json"`) are resolved recursively.

---

## The Build Pipeline (Content-Addressable Memory)

Strvct uses a **Content-Addressable Memory (CAM)** build system. The build process scans the root `_imports.json` tree and generates runtime resource bundles in the `build/` directory.

<svg viewBox="0 0 820 170" width="820" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <style>
    text { font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; fill: #111; }
    .b { font-weight: 600; }
    .dim { fill: #666; }
    .box { fill: none; stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; }
    .fill { fill: #f0ede5; stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; }
    .flow { stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; fill: none; }
  </style>
  <defs>
    <marker id="ags" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto">
      <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="#111"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <rect class="box" x="25" y="20" width="240" height="50"/>
  <text x="40" y="40" class="b">_imports.json Tree</text>
  <text x="40" y="58" class="dim">Root &amp; nested source imports</text>

  <line class="flow" x1="265" y1="45" x2="290" y2="45" marker-end="url(#ags)"/>

  <rect class="fill" x="290" y="20" width="240" height="50"/>
  <text x="305" y="40" class="b">ImportsIndexer</text>
  <text x="305" y="58" class="dim">Scans paths &amp; SHA-256 hashes</text>

  <line class="flow" x1="530" y1="45" x2="555" y2="45" marker-end="url(#ags)"/>

  <rect class="fill" x="555" y="20" width="240" height="50"/>
  <text x="570" y="40" class="b">build/ Catalog</text>
  <text x="570" y="58" class="dim">_index.json &amp; _cam.json.zip</text>

  <line class="flow" x1="675" y1="70" x2="675" y2="85"/>
  <line class="flow" x1="410" y1="85" x2="675" y2="85"/>
  <line class="flow" x1="410" y1="85" x2="410" y2="100" marker-end="url(#ags)"/>

  <rect class="box" x="290" y="100" width="240" height="50"/>
  <text x="305" y="120" class="b">Browser Runtime</text>
  <text x="305" y="138" class="dim">SvResourceManager &amp; HashCache</text>
</svg>

### Running the Build Command:
To run the source code indexer manually:

```bash
node ./strvct/source/boot/index-builder/ImportsIndexer.js
```

To index non-code media resources (icons, audio):

```bash
node ./strvct/source/boot/index-builder/SvResourceIndexer.js ./resources/icons ./resources/sounds
```

If your project includes a `justfile`, you can run:

```bash
just build
```

---

## Running Locally

Strvct includes a lightweight local HTTP/HTTPS web server (`CliWebServer.js`).

Start the development server:

```bash
node ./strvct/webserver/CliWebServer.js --port 8000 --secure false
```

### Command Flags:
- `--port <number>`: Sets the local server port (default: `8000`).
- `--secure <true|false>`: Enables HTTPS with self-signed certificates or HTTP mode.
- `--config <path>`: Optional server configuration file path.

Open `http://localhost:8000` in your browser to load the application.

---

## Chrome DevTools & Debugging

Because Strvct evaluates source files dynamically via the CAM loader, it appends `sourceURL` annotations to evaluated scripts. This enables full native browser debugging in Chrome DevTools or Cursor/VSCode:

- **Breakpoints:** Set breakpoints directly in your source JavaScript files in Chrome DevTools Sources tab.
- **Call Stacks:** Complete stack traces map directly back to original file paths and line numbers.

### Cursor / VSCode `launch.json` Configuration:

```json
{
    "version": "0.2.0",
    "configurations": [
        {
            "type": "chrome",
            "request": "launch",
            "name": "Debug Strvct App",
            "url": "http://localhost:8000",
            "webRoot": "${workspaceFolder}"
        }
    ]
}
```

---

## Creating Your First Annotated Node

Create your first domain model class inheriting from `SvStorableNode`:

```javascript
// app/Task.js
(class Task extends SvStorableNode {

    initPrototypeSlots () {
        {
            const slot = this.newSlot("title", "New Task");
            slot.setSlotType("String");
            slot.setShouldStoreSlot(true);   // Persists to IndexedDB
            slot.setSyncsToView(true);       // Live UI updates
            slot.setCanEditInspection(true); // Editable in Property Inspector
        }
        {
            const slot = this.newSlot("isCompleted", false);
            slot.setSlotType("Boolean");
            slot.setShouldStoreSlot(true);
            slot.setSyncsToView(true);
            slot.setCanEditInspection(true);
        }
    }

    initPrototype () {
        this.setTitle("Task");
        this.setShouldStore(true);
    }

}.initThisClass());
```

Add `"app/Task.js"` to your `app/_imports.json`, run `just build`, and reload your browser. Strvct will automatically generate editable form tiles, handle local persistence, and make your task node navigable in the Miller column browser!

# Implementation Overview

Deep technical specifications for class lifecycle, slots, views, persistence, notifications, and build infrastructure.

## Introduction

This document provides a detailed engineering specification of the Strvct framework implementation. It builds directly on the high-level concepts described in the [Technical Overview](../Technical%20Overview/) and the architectural foundations in [Naked Objects](../Naked%20Objects/).

Strvct applications are composed of three primary layers: **Model**, **UI**, and **Storage**. The framework eliminates manual "glue" code by embedding structural metadata directly into model objects via **Slots** and **Slot Annotations**.

## The Object & Class System

Strvct implements a structured class initialization pattern built on top of standard ES6 class syntax.

### Class Lifecycle & Registration

Classes are defined inside an IIFE (Immediately Invoked Function Expression) and self-register using `.initThisClass()`:

```javascript
(class Character extends SvStorableNode {

    initPrototypeSlots () {
        // Declare instance slots (properties + metadata)
    }

    initPrototype () {
        // Configure class-wide prototype settings
    }

    init () {
        super.init();
        // Basic instance initialization
    }

    finalInit () {
        super.finalInit();
        // Relationship resolution & post-deserialization setup
    }

}.initThisClass());
```

#### Initialization Execution Sequence:
1. **`initPrototypeSlots()`**: Invoked automatically during class registration. Defines slots and annotations on the class prototype. *Must never call `super`.*
2. **`initPrototype()`**: Sets up prototype-wide default properties (e.g., `this.setShouldStore(true)`). *Must never call `super`.*
3. **`init()`**: Called when an object is instantiated (`new Class()`). Performs basic property initialization. Always calls `super.init()`.
4. **`finalInit()`**: Called after an object is fully instantiated or deserialized from IndexedDB. Sets up complex object references and child subnodes. Always calls `super.finalInit()`.

### Slots & Slot Annotations

Slots are Strvct's property system. Instead of raw instance fields, properties are declared in `initPrototypeSlots()`:

```javascript
initPrototypeSlots () {
    {
        const slot = this.newSlot("name", "Default Name");
        slot.setSlotType("String");
        slot.setShouldStoreSlot(true);   // Persists to IndexedDB
        slot.setSyncsToView(true);       // Emits view update notifications
        slot.setCanEditInspection(true); // Editable in Property Inspector
    }
    {
        const slot = this.newSlot("inventory", null);
        slot.setFinalInitProto(InventoryNode); // Auto-creates default instance
        slot.setIsSubnodeField(true);         // Navigable tile in inspector
    }
}
```

#### Key Slot Annotations:
- `setSlotType(typeName)`: Declares expected type (`String`, `Number`, `Boolean`, `Array`, `Object`, `ClassName`). Enforces runtime type checks on setters.
- `setShouldStoreSlot(boolean)`: Controls whether the slot value is included in serialized JSON records.
- `setSyncsToView(boolean)`: Triggers change notifications to observing views upon mutation.
- `setCanEditInspection(boolean)`: Exposes property in the modifier-click (Option+Click) live Property Inspector.
- `setIsSubnode(boolean)`: Adds slot value directly to the parent's `subnodes` array.
- `setIsSubnodeField(boolean)`: Generates a navigable field tile in the inspector hierarchy.
- `setFinalInitProto(Class)`: Auto-instantiates default child objects during `finalInit()` if no record was loaded from storage.

### Categories & Protocols

- **Categories (`initThisCategory()`):** Extend existing classes across multiple files without modifying the base definition file (e.g., `SvJsonGroup_patches.js` adding `applyJsonPatches()` to `SvJsonGroup`).
- **Protocols (`NameProtocol`):** Define required interface method stubs inheriting from `Protocol` to enable runtime interface compliance checks.

---

## Model Layer Engineering

### Node Hierarchy
The domain model is an object graph inheriting from `SvNode`. Every node contains:
- `subnodes`: An ordered, unique collection of child `SvNode` objects.
- `parentNode`: Reference to the parent `SvNode`.
- `title` / `subtitle`: String properties displayed in summary tiles.
- `puuid`: Persistent unique identifier string.

### Subnode Patterns
1. **Stored Subnodes (`setIsSubnode(true)`):** Permanent parent-child ownership relationships where child nodes are stored directly inside the parent's `subnodes` array and persisted together.
2. **Subnode Fields (`setIsSubnodeField(true)`):** Properties where value state remains in a slot on the parent node, but a navigable field tile (`SvField`) is generated in the UI for inspecting child subnodes.

---

## View Layer Architecture

### Layered Class Hierarchy
The view system uses a deep, single-inheritance hierarchy where each layer adds a isolated capability:

```
SvElementDomView        (Wraps DOM element, enables alternative render backends)
 └─ SvCssDomView         (Manages inline CSS styles and class list)
     └─ SvSubviewsDomView  (Manages child view hierarchy)
         └─ SvListenerDomView (Event listener attachment)
             └─ SvVisibleDomView  (Viewport visibility tracking)
                 └─ SvGesturableDomView (Gesture recognizers: tap, pan, swipe, long-press)
                     └─ SvResponderDomView  (Focus management & keyboard navigation)
                         └─ SvControlDomView    (Target/Action pattern for control triggers)
                             └─ SvStyledDomView     (State-based style states: selected, active, disabled)
                                 └─ SvNodeView          (Binds model SvNode to DOM presentation)
```

### Navigation Primitives (Miller Columns)

The UI is rendered using nested Miller Column container views:

1. **`SvStackView`**: Core navigation container. Contains a `SvNavView` (master column) and `otherView` (detail area). Automatically collapses on mobile viewports into a push/pop stack with breadcrumbs.
2. **`SvBrowserView`**: Top-level application shell extending `SvStackView` with header breadcrumb navigation.
3. **`SvNavView`**: Single navigation column containing header, scrollable `SvTilesView`, and footer.
4. **`SvTilesView`**: Scrollable container for `SvTile` items. Handles keyboard cursor selection, drag-and-drop, and reordering gestures.
5. **`SvTile`**: Visual presentation of a single model node or property slot.

---

## Storage Layer Engineering

### Persistent Object Pools (`SvPersistentObjectPool`)
Application data is stored locally in IndexedDB as object pools (one pool per document):

- **Row Key Format:** `poolId` + `puuid` (Persistent UUID).
- **In-Pool References:** `{ "*": puuid }` (near references within the same document pool).
- **Cross-Pool References:** `{ "**": poolId }` (far references to external document roots, loaded asynchronously).

### Transactional Persistence Lifecycle
1. **Mutation Tracking:** Modifying a slot marked `setShouldStoreSlot(true)` invokes `didMutate()`, marking the node dirty.
2. **Event Loop Commit:** At the end of the current browser event loop, all dirty nodes are bundled into a single atomic IndexedDB transaction.
3. **Deserialization Pipeline:** On load, `instanceFromRecordInStore()` instantiates a blank object, invokes `init()`, populates slot state via `loadFromRecord()`, and executes `finalInit()` to reconnect object references.
4. **Garbage Collection:** Traces the stored graph from the pool root. Unreachable records are automatically deleted.
5. **SHA-256 Blob Pool (`SvBlobPool`):** Large binary assets (images, audio, files) are stored in a content-addressable store keyed by SHA-256 hash. Records store hash references rather than binary payloads.

---

## Synchronization Infrastructure

Strvct provides loose coupling across layers using three notification utilities:

1. **`SvNotificationCenter`**: Asynchronous notification dispatch. Nodes post named notifications; observing views register to handle them.
2. **`SvSyncScheduler`**: Coalesces multiple notification method invocations in one event loop into a single UI sync pass.
3. **`SvBroadcaster`**: Immediate, synchronous event broadcast for high-frequency internal events.

---

## Content-Addressable Build System (CAM)

Strvct avoids standard ES module imports and Webpack/Vite bundlers, using a custom **Content-Addressable Memory (CAM)** build system:

1. **`ImportsIndexer` (Build Time):** Recursively walks `_imports.json` files to discover source files and dependency order. Outputs:
   - `_index.json`: Metadata catalog mapping resource paths to SHA-256 content hashes.
   - `_cam.json.zip`: Zip-compressed content bundle keyed by SHA-256 hash.

2. **`SvResourceManager` & `SvHashCache` (Runtime):**
   - Fetches `_index.json` on app boot.
   - Scans missing hashes against IndexedDB `SvHashCache`.
   - If missing ratio $> 30\%$, downloads `_cam.json.zip` in one HTTP request.
   - If missing ratio $\le 30\%$, fetches individual missing files on demand.
   - Evaluates source files in dependency order via `eval()` with embedded `sourceURL` comments for complete DevTools debugging support.

# Inspectors and Debugging

Built-in tools for live Property Inspection, Developer Mode graph toggles, and Chrome DevTools source debugging.

## Overview

Because STRVCT generates user interfaces from annotated model nodes, the framework can automatically derive an **alternate Property Inspector view** for any domain object.

- **Option-Click (Alt-Click):** Option-clicking any tile opens its **Property Inspector** in the next column—a dynamically generated field tile stack displaying declared property slots, values, types, and editability flags.
- **Option-Shift-D (Alt-Shift-D):** Toggles **Developer Mode** globally (`SvApp.shared().developerMode()`), revealing hidden diagnostic subnodes, raw state inspectors, and AI message logs.

---

## Option-Click: Property Inspector

Holding **Option** while clicking any tile opens an inspector view in the next column instead of navigating to the node's standard subnodes.

### Mechanism & Implementation (`SvInspectableNode`):
1. **Gesture Interception:** The tile gesture handler (`SvTile.justAlternateTap()`) catches the Option-Click gesture and sets `isInspecting = true` on the tile.
2. **Inspector Generation:** `SvInspectableNode.nodeInspector()` clones an inspector node and populates it via `setupInspectorFromSlots()`.
3. **Slot Map Inspection:** `setupInspectorFromSlots()` walks `allSlotsMap()` down the node's class inheritance chain, instantiating an `SvFieldTile` for every slot where `slot.canInspect()` returns `true`.
4. **Live Write-Through:** Edits made inside the inspector write directly through to the live object node, automatically triggering IndexedDB persistence and view change notifications.

### Inspector Slot Annotations:
- `slot.setCanEditInspection(true)`: Controls whether the slot value is editable in place inside the inspector.
- `slot.setInspectorPath("Section/Subsection")`: Groups slots into collapsible inspector section headers.

---

## Option-Shift-D: Developer Mode

Pressing **Option+Shift+D** anywhere in `SvBrowserView` toggles `SvApp.shared().developerMode()`. The app posts an `onAppDeveloperModeChangedNote` notification when toggled.

### Opt-In Subnode Visibility Code Pattern:

Domain nodes register to observe the notification and show or hide diagnostic subnodes:

```javascript
(class Character extends SvStorableNode {

    init () {
        super.init();
        this.watchForNote("onAppDeveloperModeChangedNote");
    }

    onAppDeveloperModeChangedNote (/*aNote*/) {
        const devMode = this.app().developerMode();
        this.diagnosticsNode().setIsVisible(devMode);
        this.rawStateNode().setIsVisible(devMode);
        this.aiMessageHistory().setIsVisible(devMode);
    }

}.initThisClass());
```

# Inspirations

Frameworks and ideas that shaped STRVCT's design.

## Miller Columns

The default navigation pattern — a horizontal stack of nested tile lists — draws from Miller columns, created by Mark S. Miller in 1980 and closely related to the class hierarchy browser in Smalltalk-76. The pattern appeared in the Macintosh Finder, the NeXTSTEP File Viewer, and later macOS's column view. The NeXTSTEP implementation was the primary inspiration — its combination of columnar navigation with an object-oriented framework made the pattern feel natural for browsing object hierarchies, not just file systems. This provides spatial context as users navigate deeper into a node hierarchy, with each level visible alongside its parent.

STRVCT extends the classic Miller column pattern by allowing each level in the stack to independently choose its layout direction — vertical or horizontal — controlled by the node via `setNodeIsVertical()`. This recursive variant means a horizontal stack can contain a column whose subnodes lay out vertically, which in turn contains a row whose subnodes lay out horizontally, and so on. The alternating directions let the same navigation model serve both hierarchical browsing (vertical lists) and detail views (horizontal field layouts) without switching interaction paradigms.

## Smalltalk, Self, and Objective-C

STRVCT's object model draws from the Smalltalk tradition. Naming follows Smalltalk conventions — camelCase with `_ivar` / `ivar()` / `setIvar()` accessors. Objects are created via `clone()` rather than constructors, reflecting Self's prototype-based model. The category system, which extends classes without modifying their source files, comes directly from Objective-C (and before that, Smalltalk). The slot system for declaring instance variables echoes Smalltalk's explicit ivar declarations, and the notification center pattern traces back to Smalltalk's change/update mechanism.

## Cocoa and UIKit

The application framework layer is heavily influenced by Apple's Cocoa and UIKit:

- **Notification center** — `SvNotificationCenter` with observations mirrors `NSNotificationCenter` closely, providing publish/subscribe communication between loosely coupled components.
- **Responder chain** — `SvResponderDomView` implements `becomeFirstResponder()`, `releaseFirstResponder()`, `acceptsFirstResponder`, and `nextKeyView`, mapping directly to Cocoa's `NSResponder` / UIKit's `UIResponder` model for keyboard focus and event routing.
- **Gesture recognizers** — `SvTapGestureRecognizer`, `SvPanGestureRecognizer`, `SvPinchGestureRecognizer`, and `SvLongPressGestureRecognizer` follow the UIKit `UIGestureRecognizer` pattern, including centralized arbitration of competing gestures via `SvGestureManager`.
- **Delegate pattern** — Used throughout for communication between views, listeners, and gesture recognizers, following Cocoa's preference for delegation over subclassing.


---

<!-- Page: docs/Internationalization -->
Source: /docs/Internationalization/

# Internationalization

AI-powered translation of UI text with per-language IndexedDB persistence, batched requests, and content filtering.

## Overview

STRVCT includes a built-in internationalization (i18n) system that translates UI strings on the fly using AI language models. Rather than maintaining static, hand-edited translation files for each language, the framework sends batched translation requests to an AI service and caches the results persistently in per-language IndexedDB databases.

This approach is uniquely enabled by the naked objects pattern. Because the framework generates the UI from model slot annotations, there is a single point—the **model-to-view boundary**—where all display text passes through. Translation is injected at that boundary, making every model class translatable by default with no per-component wiring. In a bespoke-view framework, every component would need explicit `t()` calls and separate translation key files.

The system is designed around three core principles:
- **Non-blocking:** Translations happen asynchronously. The UI displays English text immediately and swaps in the translated version when it arrives, with no visible delay on subsequent visits thanks to persistent caching.
- **Smart filtering:** Numbers, currency amounts, codes, URLs, emails, and other non-linguistic content are detected and skipped automatically, avoiding unnecessary API calls.
- **Batched and deduplicated:** Individual translation requests are debounced, grouped by context, and sent as a single batch to minimize API usage.

---

## Core Architecture & Classes

The i18n system consists of five core classes in `source/library/i18n/`:

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `SvI18n` | Singleton coordinator. Manages dedicated per-language IndexedDBs, language state, deduplicates pending promises, and exposes computed status getters (`queuedCount`, `completedCount`) for admin UI. |
| `SvI18nCache` | Eager in-memory cache. Owns `i18nTranslations/cache/{lang}` IndexedDB. Loads all language entries into a `Map` on language selection. Handles seed entries (permanent) and runtime additions with FIFO eviction. |
| `SvI18nStore` | Async IndexedDB bridge (`i18nTranslations/store/{lang}`). Purely an async read/write interface to IndexedDB with no in-memory state; promotes hits to `SvI18nCache`. |
| `SvI18nService` | Batched request service. Accumulates requests for 200ms, groups by context, sends JSON templates to AI chat models, and stores results. |
| `SvTranslationFilter` | Pluggable filter with named regex functions in a Map. Determines whether a string contains translatable linguistic content. |
| `SvTranslatableNode` | Base class for translatable domain nodes (`SvNode` hierarchy). Holds per-node Tier 0 `translationMap`. |

---

## The 4-Tier Lookup Pipeline

When a view calls `node.translatedValueOfSlotNamed("slotName")`:

1. **Request & Filter Verification:** `SvTranslatableNode` checks whether translation is needed:
   - System is enabled and language is not English (`SvI18n.shared().currentLanguage() !== "en"`).
   - Text is 20 words or fewer for slot values.
   - `SvTranslationFilter.shared().shouldTranslate(text)` confirms text contains linguistic content (not numbers, URLs, codes, or emails).
2. **Tier 0: Node Map (Sync $O(1)$):** Checks `node.translationMap` (per-node FIFO `Map` capped at 10 items). Auto-clears lazily if language has changed since last access. On hit, returns immediately with no UI flicker.
3. **Tier 1: SvI18nCache Map (Sync $O(1)$):** Checks `SvI18n.cachedTranslate(text, context)`. On hit, promotes result to Tier 0 map and returns.
4. **Tier 2: SvI18nStore IndexedDB (Async):** Calls `SvI18n.asyncTranslate(text, context)`. On hit in `i18nTranslations/store/{lang}`, promotes result to Tier 1 cache and Tier 0 map, then resolves promise.
5. **Tier 3: AI Batch Translation:** On complete miss, enqueues text in `SvI18nService`:
   - Returns English source text as immediate fallback.
   - Deduplicates: if key is pending, caller promise chains onto existing request.
   - Accumulates requests for 200ms (configurable `debounceMs`), groups by context, and sends 1 AI batch JSON request.
   - Stores response in Tier 1 cache and Tier 2 store, resolves pending promises, and calls `didUpdateNode()` to swap UI text cleanly without flicker.

---

## Smart Non-Linguistic Filtering (`SvTranslationFilter`)

`SvTranslationFilter` uses a pluggable Map of named filter functions to skip unnecessary API calls:

| Filter Name | Pattern Examples Skipped |
|---|---|
| `noAlphabetical` | `17 (+3)`, `+5 / +3 / +2`, `---` |
| `numericAndCurrency` | `42`, `$9.99`, `€100`, `$70.16 USD`, `100%` |
| `alphanumericCodes` | `23A`, `#7`, `3d6`, `+5`, `10/20` |
| `ordinals` | `1st`, `2nd`, `3rd` |
| `labeledNumeric` | `HP: 45`, `AC: 18`, `XP: 1,200` |
| `emailAddresses` | `user@example.com` |
| `phoneNumbers` | `+1 (555) 123-4567` |
| `urlsAndIps` | `https://example.com`, `192.168.1.1` |

Custom domain filters can be registered dynamically:

```javascript
SvTranslationFilter.shared().addFilter("diceNotation", s => /^\d*d\d+(\s*[+-]\s*\d+)?$/i.test(s));
```

---

## Seed Generation & Cloud Storage Workflow

Seed files provide instant, cold-start translations. They group entries by context:

```json
{
    "meta": { "language": "es", "entryCount": 150 },
    "entries": {
        "ui-label": { "Hit Points": "Puntos de Golpe" },
        "game-mechanic": { "Saving Throw": "Tirada de Salvacion" }
    }
}
```

### 3-Phase Seed Generation Pipeline (Admin UI):

1. **Phase 1 — Introspection (Init Seed):**
   - Clears cache for current language.
   - Walks all `SvNode` subclass prototypes via introspection.
   - Collects labels, placeholders, valid values, and default strings for slots with `shouldTranslate() === true`.
   - Filters collected strings through `SvTranslationFilter` and enqueues them for AI batch translation.
2. **Phase 2 — Runtime Accumulation:**
   - Developers browse the UI to trigger translations for dynamic strings not discoverable via static introspection (computed titles, subtitles, dynamic action labels).
3. **Phase 3 — Cloud Upload (Store Current Seed):**
   - Exports all cache entries for the language, strips timestamps (marking entries as permanent seed entries), and uploads the JSON seed file to Firebase Storage.

---

## Configuration & Tuning Parameters

```javascript
// Change active language (ISO 639-1)
SvI18n.shared().setCurrentLanguage("es");

// Enable or disable translation system
SvI18n.shared().setIsEnabled(true);
```

### `SvI18nService` Tuning Parameters:
- `debounceMs`: Milliseconds to accumulate requests before sending batch (default: `200`).
- `maxBatchSize`: Maximum strings per API request (default: `50`).
- `maxConcurrent`: Maximum simultaneous API requests (default: `3`).

---

## View Integration Details

- **Field Tiles (`SvFieldTile`):** Calls `node.translatedValueOfSlotNamed()` in `visibleKey()`, automatically displaying translated field labels.
- **Breadcrumb Navigation (`SvBreadCrumbsTile`):** Observes `"svI18nLanguageChanged"` notification, rebuilding breadcrumb path segments in the new language.
- **Custom Views:** Any view can observe `"svI18nLanguageChanged"` to trigger a UI refresh when the active language changes.

# Lifecycle

Boot sequence, node initialization, view synchronization, and persistence cycles.

The core design challenge is that the same object must work whether it is freshly created or loaded from storage. A single-phase constructor can't handle both cases — if it creates default child objects, it will overwrite data that was just deserialized. STRVCT solves this with a three-phase sequence: `init()` sets up primitives and slot defaults, `finalInit()` creates complex child objects only if they weren't already loaded from the store, and `afterInit()` runs once the full object graph is ready. This separation means persistence is transparent — a class doesn't need different code paths for "new" vs. "loaded."

  
    text { font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; fill: #111; }
    .b { font-weight: 600; }
    .dim { fill: #666; }
    .box { fill: none; stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; }
    .fill { fill: #f0ede5; stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; }
    .flow { stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; fill: none; }
  
  
    
      
    
  
  
  ProtoClass.clone()
  or load from store
  - 
  
  1. init()
  primitive values, slot defaults;
  no object relationships yet
  - 
  
  2. finalInit()
  creates child objects via setFinalInitProto
  only if not already loaded from store
  - 
  
  3. afterInit()
  runs once the full object graph is in place

- App Lifecycle

- Persistence Lifecycle
- Headless Execution

# App Lifecycle

`SvApp` singleton initialization sequence, extension points, runtime environment hooks, user alert routing, and UI readiness promises.

## Overview

`SvApp` is the application singleton. It owns the persistent object pool, root model object graph, and top-level user interface (`SvUserInterface`). Subclasses override a small set of hook methods to initialize application models and user interfaces in a clean, predictable order.

---

## Extension Point Hook Methods

| Hook Method | When Executed | Purpose & Usage |
|---|---|---|
| `setupModel()` | Object pool store is open; root model exists. | Initialize application data models; create or fetch top-level subnodes. |
| `setupUi()` | Model object graph is ready. | Customize top-level UI presentation and window settings. |
| `appDidInit()` | Everything is wired up and live. | Post-initialization tasks; posts `"appDidInit"` notification. |
| `afterAppUiDidInit()` | UI elements are mounted and visible. | Parse URL search parameters via `handleSearchParams(params)`. |
| `handleSearchParams(params)` | Called automatically from `afterAppUiDidInit()`. | Process URL query parameters for deep-linking. |

### Top-Level Root Subnode Persistence (`rootSubnodeWithTitleForProto`):
To instantiate top-level application root nodes safely across reloads:

```javascript
setupModel () {
    super.setupModel();
    // Creates on first run; reuses from storage on subsequent loads
    this._tasksNode = this.rootSubnodeWithTitleForProto("Tasks", TaskManagerNode);
}
```

---

## Waiting for Initialization & UI Readiness

### 1. App Initialization Promise (`didInitPromise`)
Code that needs to wait for complete application setup awaits `didInitPromise()`:

```javascript
await SvApp.shared().didInitPromise();
// App is now fully initialized and live
```

### 2. UI Readiness Promise (`promiseUserInterfaceReady`)
UI-dependent code (e.g. sending navigation selection requests) awaits `promiseUserInterfaceReady()`:

```javascript
const ui = await SvApp.shared().promiseUserInterfaceReady();
if (ui.providesNavigation()) {
    // Safe to send navigation requests
    this.postNoteNamed("onRequestSelectNodePath", { path: ["Workspace", "Tasks"] });
}
```

---

## Runtime Environment Event Hooks

`SvApp` captures environment lifecycle signals and translates them into environment-agnostic hooks on `SvModel`:

| Model Hook Method (`SvModel`) | Browser Signal Event | Headless Signal Event | Purpose & Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `onAppDidGoOnline()` | `online` event | — | Network connectivity restored |
| `onAppDidGoOffline()` | `offline` event | — | Network connectivity lost |
| `onAppWillSuspend()` | `visibilitychange` (hidden) | — | App backgrounded; flush volatile state |
| `onAppWillTerminate()` | `beforeunload` (sync) | `SIGTERM` / `SIGINT` | Shutdown/unload cleanup. Return `true` to block unload. |

---

## Model User Alerts (`onRequestUserAlert`)

Domain models request user notifications without referencing UI or DOM classes:

```javascript
this.postNoteNamed("onRequestUserAlert", {
    name: "syncFailure",
    title: "Sync Error",
    message: "Failed to sync changes with cloud store.",
    level: "error" // "info" | "warning" | "error"
});
```

`SvUserInterface` observes `onRequestUserAlert`. In the browser (`SvWebUserInterface`), it opens an `SvPanelView` overlay; in headless Node.js, it logs the alert to console.

---

# Boot Sequence

How the application loads from first script tag to a running app.

## Overview

The boot process has three phases: load the boot loader, load all resources via the content-addressable memory system, then create and run the app. Each phase completes fully before the next begins, so by the time application code runs, every class and resource is available.

    .flow { stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; fill: none; }
  </style>

    </marker>
  </defs>

  <rect class="box" x="40" y="424" width="740" height="214"/>
  <text x="55" y="446" class="b">3. App Creation</text>
  <text x="55" y="464" class="dim">SvApp.loadAndRunShared()</text>
  <rect class="fill" x="55" y="479" width="710" height="34"/>
  <text x="70" y="499" class="dim">Open persistent store; load root object from store</text>
  <rect class="fill" x="55" y="517" width="710" height="34"/>
  <text x="70" y="537" class="dim">Pause schedulers; setupModel(); setupUi()</text>
  <rect class="fill" x="55" y="555" width="710" height="34"/>
  <text x="70" y="575" class="dim">appDidInit fires: post notification, unhide root view, handle URL params</text>
  <rect class="fill" x="55" y="593" width="710" height="34"/>
  <text x="70" y="613" class="dim">Resume schedulers</text>
  <text x="410" y="675" text-anchor="middle" class="dim">Each phase completes before the next; application code runs only after every class and resource is available.</text>
</svg>

## 1. Initial Bootstrap

The browser loads the boot loader script. Core boot files are loaded in parallel and evaluated sequentially. These include: Object extensions, Promise extensions, IndexedDB support, HashCache, and ResourceManager.

## 2. Resource Loading

`ResourceManager.shared().setupAndRun()` drives this phase:

1. Loads `_index.json` containing resource metadata and content hashes.
2. Checks `HashCache` for cached resources — unchanged content is never re-downloaded.
3. Downloads `_cam.json.zip` (compressed content bundle) on cache miss.
4. Evaluates CSS resources sequentially (cascade order matters).
5. Filters out environment-inappropriate resources (e.g., `browser-only/` files in Node.js) via `StrvctFile.canUseInCurrentEnv()`.
6. Evaluates JavaScript resources in dependency order.

After this phase, all classes are defined and available globally. See [Headless Execution](../Headless%20Execution/) for details on how the boot sequence adapts to Node.js.

## 3. App Creation

`SvApp.loadAndRunShared()` creates the app singleton and opens the persistent store:

```
SvApp.loadAndRunShared()
  ├── setStore(defaultStore())
  ├── loadFromStore()
  │   ├── store.promiseOpen()
  │   └── store.rootOrIfAbsentFromClosure()
  └── run()
      └── setup()
          ├── pauseSchedulers()
          ├── setupModel()
          ├── setupUi()
          ├── appDidInit()
          │   ├── setHasDoneAppInit(true)
          │   ├── postNoteNamed("appDidInit")
          │   ├── unhideRootView()
          │   └── afterAppUiDidInit()
          │       ├── handleSearchParams()
          │       └── didInitPromise.resolve()
          └── resumeSchedulers()
```

Schedulers are paused during setup so that model and UI initialization don't trigger premature sync cycles. They resume once everything is wired up.


---

<!-- Page: docs/Lifecycle/Headless Execution -->
Source: /docs/Lifecycle/Headless%20Execution/

# Headless Execution

Running STRVCT applications natively in Node.js without DOM or browser dependencies.

## Overview

STRVCT's domain model layer, persistence engine, and boot sequence execute natively in Node.js. The same application domain classes that run in the browser run headlessly under Node.js—with identical storage behavior, slot metadata annotations, and object lifecycles—just without DOM or view classes.

This enables ultra-fast unit/integration testing, server-side processing, batch simulations, and CLI tools.

<svg viewBox="0 0 820 180" width="820" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <style>

---

## Environment Detection (`SvPlatform`)

```javascript
// Environment checks
if (SvPlatform.isNodePlatform()) {
    // Node.js specific code
} else if (SvPlatform.isBrowserPlatform()) {
    // Browser specific code
}
```

---

## Directory Filtering Conventions (`browser-only` & `server-only`)

During boot resource discovery, `StrvctFile.canUseInCurrentEnv()` inspects path segments:
- In **Node.js**: Files in `browser-only/` paths are skipped.
- In **Browser**: Files in `server-only/` paths are skipped.

### The Same-Name Class Pattern:
This convention provides environment-specific implementations of the exact same class interface:

```
source/boot/browser-only/SvIndexedDbFolder.js   # Uses native IndexedDB
source/boot/server-only/SvIndexedDbFolder.js     # Uses LevelDB via classic-level
```

---

## Browser API Shims for Node.js (`server-only`)

In `source/library/ideal/categories/server-only/`:

| Shim File | Browser API Polyfilled | Node.js Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| `XMLHttpRequestShim.js` | `XMLHttpRequest` | Wraps `xhr2` package |
| `FileReaderShim.js` | `FileReader` | Reads ArrayBuffer and text from Blobs |
| `ImageShim.js` | `Image`, `HTMLCanvasElement` | Wraps `canvas` package |
| `FontFaceShim.js` | `FontFace` | Stub accepting font declarations |

---

## Storage Engine Parity

Storage works identically in both environments through `SvIndexedDbFolder`:
- **Browser:** Writes to native IndexedDB.
- **Node.js:** Writes to LevelDB (`classic-level`) in `./data/leveldb/`.
