---

## Defining a Category (`.initThisCategory()`)

```javascript
// SvJsonGroup_patches.js — adds JSON Patch methods to SvJsonGroup
(class SvJsonGroup_patches extends SvJsonGroup {

    applyJsonPatches (patches) {
        // Implementation
    }

    applyPatch (operation) {
        // Single patch operation
    }

}.initThisCategory());
```

Executing `.initThisCategory()` instructs the class registration system to merge all prototype and static methods into the parent class (`SvJsonGroup`). No new class entry is created in the global class registry.

---

## Naming Conventions & `_imports.json` Order

- **File & Class Naming:** Category files and classes use an underscore to separate the target base class name from the category purpose:
  `SvJsonGroup_patches.js`, `Array_promises.js`, `Promise_ideal.js`.
- **Import Dependency Order:** The base class **must** be listed before its category files in `_imports.json`:

```json
[
    "SvJsonGroup.js",
    "SvJsonGroup_patches.js",
    "SvJsonGroup_clientState.js"
]
```

---

## Extending JavaScript Builtins

Categories are used heavily during boot to extend native JavaScript objects without polluting the global scope with global functions:

```javascript
// Promise_ideal.js — adds clone(), status tracking, and timeouts
(class Promise_ideal extends Promise {
    static clone () { /* ... */ }
    callResolveFunc (...args) { /* ... */ }
    isPending () { /* ... */ }
}.initThisCategory());

// Array_promises.js — adds async iteration methods
(class Array_promises extends Array {
    async promiseSerialForEach (aBlock) { /* ... */ }
    async promiseParallelMap (aBlock) { /* ... */ }
}.initThisCategory());
```

---

## Category Constraints & Rules

1. **No New Slots:** Categories can only add methods—they **cannot** add new slots via `initPrototypeSlots()`, as prototype slots must be defined during initial class registration.
2. **`instanceof` Compatibility:** `instanceof` checks are completely unaffected. An instance of `SvJsonGroup` answers `true` for `instanceof SvJsonGroup` and does not add a prototype link layer.
3. **Full `this` Access:** Category methods execute with full access to `this` and all slots and methods of the base class.

---

## Related Guides

- [Protocols](../Protocols/index.html): Interface declaration and conformance checking.
- [Style Guide](../Style%20Guide/index.html): Coding standards and class patterns.

# Protocols

Declaring interfaces and verifying conformance at runtime with fail-fast registration checks.

## Overview

Protocols are STRVCT's interface system. A protocol defines a set of methods that a class promises to implement. Unlike informal duck-typing (where code checks for individual methods at call sites), protocols name the contract, support inheritance, and verify conformance at class registration time.

The defining feature of STRVCT's protocol engine is **fail-fast verification**: when a class declares conformance to a protocol via `addProtocol()`, the framework immediately verifies that all required methods exist. If any method is missing, an error is thrown at startup—moving bugs from rare runtime surprises to instant, deterministic startup failures.

<svg viewBox="0 0 820 220" width="820" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">

    .flow { stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; fill: none; }
  </style>

---

## Defining a Protocol (`.initThisProtocol()`)

A protocol inherits from `Protocol` and declares empty method stubs representing the interface:

```javascript
(class SvAudioClipProtocol extends Protocol {

    play () {
    }

    stop () {
    }

    addDelegate (audioClipDelegate) {
    }

    removeDelegate (audioClipDelegate) {
    }

}.initThisProtocol());
```

### Protocol Rules:
- Execute `.initThisProtocol()` at class registration.
- Class name **must** end with `Protocol` (enforced at startup).
- Method bodies are empty stubs defining expected parameters.

---

## Implementing & Verifying a Protocol (`addProtocol`)

Implementers call `addProtocol()` inside `initPrototype()`:

```javascript
(class SvWaSound extends SvSummaryNode {

    initPrototype () {
        this.addProtocol(SvAudioClipProtocol);
    }

    play () {
        // Implementation
    }

    stop () {
        // Implementation
    }

    addDelegate (delegate) {
        // Implementation
    }

    removeDelegate (delegate) {
        // Implementation
    }

}.initThisClass());
```

---

## Required and Optional Methods

`addProtocol()` checks only a protocol's **required** methods. A protocol names the ones an adopter may leave out with the static `optionalMethodNames()`; by default there are none, so every declared method is required.

```javascript
(class SvExampleProtocol extends Protocol {

    static optionalMethodNames () {
        return ["describe"];
    }

    play () {
    }

    describe () {
    }

}.initThisProtocol());
```

---

## Delegate Protocols

A **delegate protocol** declares the messages one kind of object sends its delegate through `sendDelegateMessage()`. A delegate implements only the messages it cares about, so a delegate protocol extends `SvDelegateProtocol`, which makes every message optional. Adopting one declares who listens; it never fails.

Name a delegate protocol after its sender (`SvHtmlStreamReader` → `SvHtmlStreamReaderDelegateProtocol`), and declare exactly what the sender sends, with the arguments it sends them with:

```javascript
(class SvHtmlStreamReaderDelegateProtocol extends SvDelegateProtocol {

    onHtmlStreamReaderPushNode (reader, node) {
    }

    // ...

}.initThisProtocol());
```

The **sender** names its protocol:

```javascript
delegateProtocol () {
    return SvHtmlStreamReaderDelegateProtocol;
}
```

and each **delegate** adopts it in `initPrototype()` with `this.addProtocol(SvHtmlStreamReaderDelegateProtocol)`.

Two checks keep the declaration and the code from drifting apart:

- **At runtime**, `sendDelegateMessage()` warns once per sender class and message when a sender that names a protocol sends a message the protocol does not declare.
- **In tests**, `tests/headless/TestDelegateProtocols.js` scans the source. Every message a sender sends must be declared, every declared message must be sent (a declared message nobody sends is an invented interface), and every delegate protocol must be named by a sender.

A protocol file loads before any class that adopts it: list it first in its folder's `_imports.json`, or in a folder that loads earlier.

---

## Protocol Verification API

| Method | Purpose & Return Value |
|---|---|
| `addProtocol(protocol)` | Registers the protocol; throws if a required method is missing. |
| `conformsToProtocol(protocol)` | `true` if the class has added the protocol. |
| `assertConformsToProtocol(protocol)` | Throws if the class has not added the protocol. |
| `methodsConformToProtocol(protocol)` | `true` if the object implements every required method. |
| `Protocol.protocolMethodNames()` | Every method the protocol declares, including those of ancestor protocols. |
| `Protocol.optionalMethodNames()` / `requiredMethodNames()` | The declared methods an adopter may leave out / must implement. |
| `Protocol.declaresMethodNamed(name)` | Whether the protocol declares the method (required or optional). |
| `Protocol.allProtocols()` | Every protocol class. |

---

## Framework Protocols

The protocol files are the source of truth. These are the ones the framework declares:

**Capabilities** (every method required, unless marked optional)

- **`SvAudioClipProtocol`:** something that plays (`play()`, `stop()`, `addDelegate()`, `removeDelegate()`).
- **`SvRecordStoreProtocol`:** a record store: local, memory or cloud.
- **`SvProgressiveImageSourceProtocol`:** a node whose image arrives in stages (aspect ratio, preview, working, failed).
- **`SvCollapsibleRegionProtocol`:** a region that expands and collapses (`isExpanded()`, `toggleExpanded()`, `collapsibleAxis()`).
- **`SvJsonSerializableProtocol`:** a node with a JSON form for AI exchange, import and export (`serializeToJson()`; `deserializeFromJson()` optional, since some nodes are only exported). Adopted by `SvJsonGroup`, `SvJsonArrayNode`, `SvJsonDictionaryNode`, `SvImageNode`, `SvDateNode`, `SvTimeNode` and `SvToolResult`; their subclasses conform through them.

An optional hook that most classes don't implement is not a protocol: it is a method on the base class with a default (`cssVariableDict()` returns null, `nodeAcceptsDrop()` false), which classes that care override. Callers then call it without checking whether it exists. See [Complete Protocols](../../Future%20Work/Complete%20Protocols/).

**Delegate protocols** (every message optional)

| Protocol | Sender | Delegates |
|---|---|---|
| `SvAudioClipDelegateProtocol` | an audio clip | `SvAudioQueue` |
| `SvHtmlStreamReaderDelegateProtocol` | `SvHtmlStreamReader` | `SvAiParsedResponseMessage` |
| `SvXhrRequestDelegateProtocol` | `SvXhrRequest` | `SvAiRequest`, `SvFileToDownload` |
| `SvAiRequestDelegateProtocol` | `SvAiRequest` | `SvAiResponseMessage` |
| `SvConversationMessageDelegateProtocol` | `SvConversationMessage` and its subclasses | `SvConversation` |
| `SvImagineProImageGenerationDelegateProtocol` | `SvImagineProImageGeneration` | — |
| `SvRzSigServerConnDelegateProtocol` | `SvRzSigServerConn` | — |
| `SvRzPeerConnDelegateProtocol` | `SvRzPeerConn` | — |

---

<!-- Page: docs/Programming Idioms/Style Guide -->
Source: /docs/Programming%20Idioms/Style%20Guide/

# Style Guide

Coding conventions, self-initializing class patterns, method chaining, and file structure rules across STRVCT.

## Overview

STRVCT follows smalltalk-inspired JavaScript coding conventions to ensure codebase consistency, high-signal readability, and predictable framework behavior.

---

## 1. Class Declaration & Self-Registration Pattern

Classes are wrapped in IIFE closures and self-register using `.initThisClass()` (or `.initThisCategory()` for categories):

```javascript
(class Character extends SvStorableNode {

    initPrototypeSlots () {
        {
            const slot = this.newSlot("name", "");
            slot.setSlotType("String");
            slot.setShouldStoreSlot(true);
            slot.setSyncsToView(true);
        }
    }

    initPrototype () {
        this.setTitle("Character");
        this.setShouldStore(true);
    }

    init () {
        super.init();
        // Basic instance setup
    }

    finalInit () {
        super.finalInit();
        // Post-deserialization relationship wiring
    }

}.initThisClass());
```

---

## 2. Naming Conventions

- **Class Names:** PascalCase with framework prefix (`SvNode`, `SvStackView`, `SvPersistentObjectPool`).
- **Category Files & Classes:** Base class name + underscore + category purpose (`SvJsonGroup_patches.js`, `Array_promises.js`).
- **Protocols:** Always end with `Protocol` (`SvAudioClipProtocol`, `SvDragSourceProtocol`).
- **Slot Getters & Setters:** Getter matches slot name (`node.name()`); setter prepends `set` (`node.setName("Thorin")`).
- **Boolean Methods:** Prepend `is`, `has`, `should`, or `can` (`node.isSubnode()`, `slot.shouldStoreSlot()`, `view.canInspect()`).

---

## 3. Chained Method Setters

All configuration setters on views and slots return `this` to allow clean method chaining:

```javascript
const view = SvDomView.clone()
    .setPosition("absolute")
    .setTop("0px")
    .setLeft("0px")
    .setWidth("100%")
    .setHeight("100%")
    .setBackgroundColor("#111");
```

---

## 4. `_imports.json` Dependency Ordering

Every folder specifies its resource list and subfolder dependencies in `_imports.json`. Base class files **must** precede category extensions or subclass files:

```json
[
    "_css.css",
    "SvNode.js",
    "SvNode_subnodes.js",
    "SvStorableNode.js"
]
```

---

## Related Guides

- [Categories](../Categories/index.html): Extending existing classes via categories.
- [Protocols](../Protocols/index.html): Interface declaration and conformance checks.
- [Async Patterns](../Async%20Patterns/index.html): Asynchronous array iteration and promise helpers.

# Classes

Complete class inheritance hierarchy.

Two naming conventions appear in this tree:
- **Categories** (`BaseClass_suffix.js`, e.g. `Array_ideal`, `SvJsonGroup_patches`) — extend a base class purely to add methods. They share their base's prototype rather than introducing a new type.
- **Protocols** (`*Protocol`, e.g. `SvAudioClipProtocol`) — interface-like classes extending `Protocol`, enumerated separately on the [Protocols](../Protocols/) page with their implementors.

- Object
  - [AiParsedResponseMessage_tagEvents](../../resources/class-doc/class_doc.html?path=%2Fsource%2Flibrary%2Fservices%2FAiServiceKit%2FParsing%2F-unused%2FAiParsedResponseMessage_tagEvents.js)
  - Array

    - [Array_mutator](../../resources/class-doc/class_doc.html?path=%2Fsource%2Flibrary%2Fideal%2Fcollections%2FSvHookedArray.js)
    - [Array_promises](../../resources/class-doc/class_doc.html?path=%2Fsource%2Fboot%2Fcategories%2FArray_promises.js)
    - [Array_store](../../resources/class-doc/class_doc.html?path=%2Fsource%2Flibrary%2Fnode%2Fstorage%2Fbase%2Fcategories%2Fprimitives%2FArray_store.js)

# Services

AI, cloud, media, and IoT service integrations.

## Overview

Services are not part of the Strvct core — they are optional integrations provided as a convenient way to quickly connect with important external services. The `Services` singleton is the root container for all of them. Each service is a standard Strvct node with slots, persistence, and automatic UI — the same patterns used for domain objects apply to service configuration. Users can inspect and configure services (API keys, model selection, proxy settings) through the generated interface without any custom settings UI.

- AI Services
- Cloud Storage
- Media
- Proxies
- Home Assistant


---

<!-- Page: docs/Services/AI Services -->
Source: /docs/Services/AI%20Services/

# AI Services

Framework architecture for multi-provider AI integration, streaming execution, tool calling, and model-first operability.

## Introduction & The Model-First AI Advantage

Strvct provides a comprehensive, multi-provider AI infrastructure built directly into the framework. Unlike traditional applications where AI integration requires writing bespoke API wrappers, per-screen tool specifications, and custom JSON serializers, Strvct's **Naked Objects** architecture makes the entire domain model **natively AI-operable** out of the box.

Because every domain class declares instance properties as **slots** with metadata annotations (`slotType`, `canEditInspection`, `isSubnodeField`), Strvct exposes a universal AI tool surface consisting of just two generic, constant-size functions:

1. **`schema-fetch`**: Inspects slot metadata to generate JSON schemas for any domain class or live object instance.
2. **`apply-patch`**: Validates and applies JSON patch payloads to mutate properties or update child relationships on live domain objects.

This tool surface remains **constant in size** whether an application contains 5 domain classes or 500. When an AI agent generates an invalid patch, the framework's rejected response returns the slot schema, enabling the LLM to self-correct in real time.

---

## Service & Request Factory Architecture

AI providers are implemented as paired service and request singletons inheriting from base infrastructure classes:

- **`SvAiService`**: High-level provider service singleton (e.g., `SvAnthropicService`, `SvGeminiService`, `SvOpenAiService`). Manages authentication, endpoint resolution, and model capability registries.
- **`SvAiRequest`**: Low-level HTTP request wrapper handling message formatting, custom headers, and streaming chunk parsing.

### Automatic Factory Resolution

`SvAiService` resolves its paired request class dynamically using naming conventions (`SvGeminiService` automatically pairs with `SvGeminiRequest`). Adding a new AI provider requires implementing the service and request subclass without registering explicit factory hooks.

### Authentication & Token Flow

Authentication is resolved via `apiKeyOrUserAuthToken()`:
1. First checks `SvCredentialManager` for a Firebase bearer token (for production apps proxying requests through Firebase Cloud Functions to protect secrets).
2. Falls back to a client-stored API key (for local development or direct user API key entry).

---

## AI Model Registry (`SvAiChatModel`)

`SvAiChatModel` represents a specific LLM model instance (e.g., `claude-3-5-sonnet`, `gemini-1.5-pro`, `gpt-4o`). Each model definition includes:

- `modelName`: Standard provider model identifier string.
- `inputTokenLimit` / `outputTokenLimit`: Context window limits.
- Capability Flags: `supportsTemperature`, `supportsTopP`, `supportsImageGeneration`, `supportsVideoGeneration`, `supportsTools`.

The global `Services` node provides global helper methods to query models across all registered providers:

```javascript
const models = Services.shared().aiServices().chatModels();
const model  = Services.shared().aiServices().chatModelWithName("claude-3-5-sonnet");
```

---

## Conversations & Messaging (`SvAiConversation` & `SvAiMessage`)

`SvAiConversation` manages conversational state, token counts, system prompts, tool call history, and active LLM chat requests.

- **`SvAiMessage`**: Extends standard conversation messages with role designations (`system`, `user`, `assistant`).
- **Role Mapping**: Provider services map generic role names to provider-specific conventions automatically (e.g., mapping `assistant` to `model` for Gemini APIs).

---

## The Assistant ToolKit & Function Execution

Structured tool calling is coordinated by `SvAssistantToolKit`:

  <rect class="box" x="440" y="100" width="240" height="50"/>
  <text x="455" y="120" class="b">Completion State Patch</text>
  <text x="455" y="138" class="dim">Mutates live domain nodes</text>
</svg>

### 1. Tool Registration
Methods on model nodes are marked as toolable during slot setup:

```javascript
const tool = this.methodNamed("rollDice");
tool.setDescription("Roll dice for a combat check");
tool.addParameter("notation", "String", "Standard dice notation like 2d6+3");
tool.setIsToolable(true);
```

### 2. Execution Timing Phases
Tools execute at specific points in the response lifecycle:
- **Streaming Phase (`onStreamData`):** Executes in real time while tokens arrive (e.g., playing a sound effect or triggering a UI animation).
- **Completion Phase (`onRequestComplete`):** Executes after the full response is validated (e.g., applying state mutations to domain nodes).
- **Narration Phase (`onPlayback`):** Executes synchronized with Text-To-Speech (TTS) voice audio playback.

---

## Incremental Streaming Response Parser (`SvAiParsedResponseMessage`)

AI responses arrive as continuous token streams. `SvAiParsedResponseMessage` parses structured XML tags incrementally during streaming without waiting for full response completion:

- `<tool-call>`: Extracted and dispatched immediately to `SvAssistantToolKit`.
- `<narration>`: Extracted and routed directly to the TTS voice audio queue for zero-latency speech synthesis.
- `<thought>` / `<quote>` / `<sentence>`: Extracted for structured UI display in chat message views.

---

## Modular Prompt Composition (`SvAiPromptComposer`)

`SvAiPromptComposer` builds complex system prompts dynamically using modular text template files without manual string concatenation in JavaScript:

```
[ Template File: SystemPrompt.txt ]
"System rules: {{file$Rules.txt}}
 Current Character: {{$characterSummary}}
 Available Actions: {{$tableOfContents}}"
```

### Supported Substitution Directives:
1. `{{file$Path/ToFile.txt}}`: Recursively embeds the contents of a secondary prompt template file.
2. `{{$methodName}}`: Executes a getter method on the target domain object and inserts the string result.
3. `{{$tableOfContents}}`: Generates a structured table of contents from headings in the prompt document.

---

## Provider Support Matrix

| Service Class | Provider | Key Capabilities & Models |
|---|---|---|
| `SvAnthropicService` | Anthropic | Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3 Opus, native tool use |
| `SvGeminiService` | Google | Gemini 1.5 Pro/Flash, text-to-video, multimodal inputs |
| `SvOpenAiService` | OpenAI | GPT-4o, DALL-E 3 image generation, TTS voice synthesis |
| `SvGroqService` | Groq | Ultra-low-latency inference (OpenAI compatible) |
| `SvDeepSeekService` | DeepSeek | DeepSeek V3 / R1 reasoning models |
| `SvXaiService` | xAI | Grok 2 models (OpenAI compatible) |
| `SvImagineProService`| ImaginePro | Midjourney image generation via proxy API |

---

## Adding a New AI Provider

To add a new AI provider, implement two classes following naming conventions:

1. **Service Subclass (`SvNewProviderService.js`):**
   ```javascript
   (class SvNewProviderService extends SvAiService {
       modelsJson () {
           return [
               { name: "new-model-v1", inputTokenLimit: 128000, outputTokenLimit: 4096 }
           ];
       }
   }.initThisClass());
   ```

2. **Request Subclass (`SvNewProviderRequest.js`):**
   ```javascript
   (class SvNewProviderRequest extends SvAiRequest {
       buildBody () {
           // Format message payload for API endpoint
       }
       readDataChunk (chunk) {
           // Parse streaming SSE chunks
       }
   }.initThisClass());
   ```

3. **Slot Registration:** Declare the new service slot in `Services.initPrototypeSlots()`. The service/request factory automatically binds `SvNewProviderService` to `SvNewProviderRequest`.

<!-- Page: docs/Services/Cloud Storage -->
Source: /docs/Services/Cloud%20Storage/

# Cloud Storage

Firebase integration for cloud persistence and file storage.

## SvFirebaseService

Integrates with Firebase for cloud persistence and file storage. Unlike AI services, `SvFirebaseService` extends `SvSummaryNode` directly and contains two sub-services:

- **`SvFirestoreDatabaseService`** — Document and collection access via Firestore. Provides query building, real-time listeners, and CRUD operations through Strvct node wrappers (`SvFirestoreNode`, `SvFirestoreQuery`).
- **`SvFirebaseStorageService`** — File upload and download via Firebase Storage, with permission management.

Document persistence does not go through these wrappers. Object pools reach the cloud through `SvCloudRecordStore`, which calls the backend's record functions (open, changes, children, commit); see [Cloud Object Pools](../../Persistence/Cloud%20Object%20Pools/).


---

<!-- Page: docs/Services/Home Assistant -->
Source: /docs/Services/Home%20Assistant/

# Home Assistant

IoT device control via Home Assistant's WebSocket API.

## Overview

The Home Assistant integration maps an entire Home Assistant instance — areas, devices, entities, and states — into the Strvct node graph. The result is a navigable, inspectable tree of your smart home that uses the same UI patterns as the rest of the framework. No custom views are involved; the generated interface lets you browse areas, drill into devices, see entity states, and inspect raw JSON from HA — all from slot annotations.

Multiple Home Assistant instances are supported. Each connection is configured with a host, port, and long-lived access token, all editable through the generated inspector.

## Connection

Communication uses the Home Assistant WebSocket API. Because browsers disallow plain `ws://` connections from HTTPS pages, a small WSS-to-WS proxy relays traffic between the browser and HA's local WebSocket endpoint.

### Authentication Flow

1. Browser opens a secure WebSocket connection to the proxy
2. HA sends `auth_required`
3. Client responds with the stored long-lived access token
4. HA replies `auth_ok` or `auth_invalid`
5. On success, a full data refresh begins

All subsequent requests use a sequential integer ID with a promise-based response pattern — each outgoing message gets a unique ID, and incoming results are matched to their pending promise by that ID.

## Data Model

After authentication, the integration fetches four registries in parallel:

| Group | HA WebSocket Command | Node Class |
|---|---|---|
| Areas | `config/area_registry/list` | `SvHomeAssistantArea` |
| SvDevices | `config/device_registry/list` | `SvHomeAssistantDevice` |
| Entities | `config/entity_registry/list` | `SvHomeAssistantEntity` |
| States | `get_states` | `SvHomeAssistantState` |

Each registry response is an array of JSON objects. For each entry, a corresponding Strvct node is created and registered in an ID map for O(1) lookup.

### Object Wiring

After all four registries are loaded, a wiring pass connects objects into a hierarchy based on their foreign keys:

- **SvDevices** attach to **Areas** via `area_id`
- **Entities** attach to **SvDevices** via `device_id`
- **States** attach to **Entities** via `entity_id`

The result is a tree rooted at a `SvHomeAssistantFolder` node (titled "regions") that mirrors the physical layout of the home:

```
Home Assistant
└── regions
    ├── Living Room (area)
    │   └── HomePod (device)
    │       └── volume (entity)
    │           └── standby (state)
    ├── Kitchen (area)
    │   └── ...
    └── ...
```

### Display Names

Each object computes a short display name by stripping its parent's name as a prefix. For example, a device named "Living Room Speaker" under the "Living Room" area displays as "Speaker". This keeps the tree compact without losing context.

## Class Hierarchy

```
SvHomeAssistants              — Collection of HA connections
 └── SvHomeAssistant          — One connection instance
      ├── rootFolder        — Navigable UI tree (regions)
      ├── SvHomeAssistantAreas     ─┐
      ├── SvHomeAssistantDevices    │ Data groups (hidden,
      ├── SvHomeAssistantEntities   │ used for ID lookup)
      └── SvHomeAssistantStates    ─┘

SvHomeAssistantGroup          — Base for the four registry groups
 ├── SvHomeAssistantAreas
 ├── SvHomeAssistantDevices
 ├── SvHomeAssistantEntities
 └── SvHomeAssistantStates

SvHomeAssistantObject         — Base for individual HA items
 ├── SvHomeAssistantArea
 ├── SvHomeAssistantDevice
 ├── SvHomeAssistantEntity
 └── SvHomeAssistantState
```

The four data group nodes (`areasNode`, `devicesNode`, `entitiesNode`, `statesNode`) are hidden from the UI — they exist for ID-based lookup during the wiring pass. The visible navigation tree is the `rootFolder`, which is populated with area nodes after all data is loaded and wired.

<!-- Page: docs/Services/Media -->
Source: /docs/Services/Media/

# Media

YouTube audio playback and browser speech recognition.

## SvYouTubeService

Manages YouTube-based audio playback via the IFrame Player API. The service contains a `SvYouTubeAudioPlayer` subnode that wraps a hidden YouTube player element.

### SvYouTubeAudioPlayer

The core playback class. Handles player lifecycle, volume, looping, and state tracking. The YouTube IFrame API script is loaded lazily on first use, and playback waits for a user gesture (browser autoplay policy).

```javascript
// Create a player and loop background music
const player = SvYouTubeAudioPlayer.clone();
player.setTrackName("Ambient Forest");
player.setVideoId("abc123xyz");
player.setShouldRepeat(true);
player.setVolume(0.1);
player.play();

// Control
player.stop();
player.togglePlay();
player.isPlaying();       // => boolean
player.stateName();       // => "playing" | "paused" | "buffering" | "ended"

// One-shot playback (resolves when video ends)
player.setShouldRepeat(false);
await player.play();

// Cleanup
await player.shutdown();  // destroys the YT.Player and removes the DOM element
```

### SvMusicLibrary

A higher-level layer that manages playlists of `SvMusicTrack` nodes loaded from a JSON resource file. Owns two `SvYouTubeAudioPlayer` instances — one for background music (low volume), one for sound effects (higher volume).

```javascript
// Play looping background music by track name
library.playTrackWithName("Mystical Forest");

// Play a one-shot sound effect
await library.playSoundEffectWithName("Sword Clash");

// Stop background music
library.musicPlayer().stop();

// Lookup
library.trackWithName("Battle Theme");       // => SvMusicTrack
library.playlists();                          // => SvMusicFolder[]
library.trackNames();                         // => String[]
```

Playlist data is a JSON object mapping folder names to track dictionaries:

```json
{
  "Fantasy": {
    "Mystical Forest": "YouTubeVideoId1",
    "Battle Theme": "YouTubeVideoId2"
  },
  "Sound FX": {
    "Sword Clash": "YouTubeVideoId3"
  }
}
```

### SvMusicTrack

Represents a single track with a YouTube video ID. Supports a delegate set for playback notifications:

```javascript
track.addDelegate(myObserver);
await track.play();
track.stop();
```

Delegates receive `onSoundStarted(track)` and `onSoundEnded(track)`.

## SvSpeechToTextSessions

Wraps the browser's native `SpeechRecognition` API for voice input. Each `SvSpeechToTextSession` tracks recognition state, language settings, and transcription results. Not a cloud service — all processing happens in the browser.

### SvSpeechToTextSession

```javascript
const session = SvSpeechToTextSession.clone();
session.setDelegate(myObject);
session.setLanguage("en-US");
session.setIsContinuous(true);
session.setGetInterimResults(true);
session.setInputTimeoutMs(1500);

// Start — returns a promise that resolves with the transcript
// when the input timeout fires (silence detected after speech)
const text = await session.start();

// Manual stop
session.stop();

// State
session.isRecording();
session.fullTranscript();       // accumulated text
session.interimTranscript();    // current partial text
```

### Delegate Protocol

All methods are optional. The session is passed as the first argument.

| Method | When |
|---|---|
| `onSpeechInterimResult(session)` | Partial result received |
| `onSpeechFinal(session)` | Finalized segment received, appended to `fullTranscript` |
| `onSpeechEnd(session)` | Browser speech recognition ended |
| `onSpeechInput(session)` | Input timeout elapsed — transcript is final |
| `onSessionEnd(session)` | Recognition service disconnected |
| `onSpeechError(session, error)` | Recognition error |

### Usage in SvTextView

Any text field supports voice input via Alt+L. Holding the key starts a session; releasing it stops recognition and inserts the transcript at the cursor:

```javascript
startSpeechToText () {
    this._speechSession = SvSpeechToTextSession.clone().setDelegate(this);
    this._speechSession.start();
}

onSpeechEnd (speechSession) {
    const s = speechSession.fullTranscript();
    this.insertTextAtCursorSimple(s);
    this._speechSession = null;
}
```


---

<!-- Page: docs/Services/Proxies -->
Source: /docs/Services/Proxies/

# Proxies

Client-side proxy configuration for routing API calls through intermediary servers.

## Overview

These classes do not run proxy servers — they are client-side configuration nodes that store proxy server connection details and rewrite API URLs to route through a proxy. The actual proxy server (e.g. a Firebase Function or local HTTPS reverse proxy) runs separately.

The primary use case is routing AI service API calls through a proxy that holds the real API keys, so that browser clients never see provider credentials directly. The client sends a Firebase user auth token to the proxy, and the proxy adds the appropriate API key before forwarding the request.

## SvProxyServers

`SvProxyServers` is a singleton collection of `SvProxyServer` entries, accessible via `SvProxyServers.shared()`. In practice, a single `SvDefaultProxyServer` entry handles all routing, accessible via `SvProxyServers.shared().defaultServer()`.

Users can add, remove, and reorder proxy entries through the generated inspector UI. All entries are persisted to IndexedDB.

## SvProxyServer

Each `SvProxyServer` node stores the connection details for one proxy endpoint:

| Slot | Type | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isSecure` | Boolean | `true` | Use `https` or `http` |
| `subdomain` | String | `""` | Optional subdomain prefix |
| `domain` | String | `""` | Base domain (e.g. `localhost`, `example.com`) |
| `port` | Number | `0` | Port number (0 or null omits port from URL) |
| `path` | String | `""` | URL path (e.g. `/proxy`) |
| `parameterName` | String | `null` | Query parameter name for the target URL |
| `isDisabled` | Boolean | `false` | When true, returns target URLs unchanged |

All configuration slots are persisted and editable through the generated inspector.

### URL Rewriting

The core method is `proxyUrlForUrl(targetUrl)`, which rewrites a direct API URL into a proxied one:

```
Target:  https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions
Proxied: https://localhost:8443/proxy?proxyUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.openai.com%2Fv1%2Fchat%2Fcompletions
```

The target URL is passed as a query parameter (named by `parameterName`), so the proxy server can decode it, forward the request to the real provider, and stream the response back.

If `isDisabled` is true, the target URL is returned unchanged — useful for direct API access during development.

## SvDefaultProxyServer

`SvDefaultProxyServer` extends `SvProxyServer` and auto-configures itself from the browser's current page URL on startup. For a page served at `https://localhost:8443`, it defaults to:

- `isSecure`: `true`
- `hostname`: `localhost`
- `port`: `8443`
- `path`: `/proxy`
- `parameterName`: `"proxyUrl"`

This means the proxy is assumed to run on the same origin as the application by default. Applications can override these settings programmatically via `setupForConfigDict()` using build-time environment configuration.

## Integration with AI Services

`SvAiRequest` has a `needsProxy` slot (default `true`). When making an API call, the request checks this flag and rewrites the URL if needed:

```javascript
async activeApiUrl () {
    let url = this.apiUrl();  // e.g. "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions"
    if (this.needsProxy()) {
        url = SvProxyServers.shared().defaultServer().proxyUrlForUrl(url);
    }
    return url;
}
```

This applies to all AI service requests (chat, image generation, text-to-speech, video generation) and also to image/media downloads that would otherwise be blocked by CORS in production.

# Slots

The property system: declaration, slot annotations, runtime type checks, lifecycle hooks, and metadata consumers.

## Overview

Slots are Strvct's property system. In traditional JavaScript objects, instance fields are simple key-value pairs without metadata. In Strvct, declaring a property as a **slot** transforms it into a rich metadata carrier that each framework layer reads independently.

<svg viewBox="0 0 820 220" width="820" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">

    .fill { fill: #f0ede5; stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; }
    .flow { stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; fill: none; }
  </style>
  <defs>

      <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="#111"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <!-- Row 1: Centered Slot Metadata Box (w: 240, h: 50) -->

  <text x="410" y="195" text-anchor="middle" class="dim">Slots decouple business logic from UI, persistence, and AI tools; declare metadata once, every layer benefits automatically.</text>
</svg>

---

## Declaration Syntax & Slot Maps

Slots are declared inside `initPrototypeSlots()` during class registration. Declaring a slot installs a private variable (`_slotName`), an auto-generated getter (`slotName()`), and an auto-generated setter (`setSlotName(value)`) on the class prototype.

Each class prototype maintains two slot maps:
- **`slotsMap()`**: Map of slots defined directly on this specific class.
- **`allSlotsMap()`**: Map of all slots from this class and every ancestor class, accumulated down the prototype chain.

```javascript
(class Character extends SvStorableNode {

    initPrototypeSlots () {
        {
            const slot = this.newSlot("name", "");
            slot.setSlotType("String");
            slot.setShouldStoreSlot(true);   // Included in IndexedDB record rows
            slot.setSyncsToView(true);       // Posts didChangeSlot notification
            slot.setCanEditInspection(true); // Editable field in Property Inspector
        }
        {
            const slot = this.newSlot("ownerNode", null);
            slot.setIsWeak(true);            // WeakRef memory safety
            slot.setSyncsToView(true);
        }
    }

}.initThisClass());
```

---

## Complete Annotation Setters Table

| Setter Method | Default | Purpose / Subsystem Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| `setSlotType("String")` | `"Object"` | Controls type validation, form field input type, and LLM JSON schema generation. |
| `setIsWeak(true)` | `false` | Holds value via `WeakRef` to prevent retain cycles in parent/owner back references. |
| `setIsLazy(true)` | `false` | Defers initialization or loading until the first getter call. |
| `setShouldStoreSlot(true)` | `false` | Instructs `SvObjectPool` to include property in serialized IndexedDB record rows. |
| `setIsInCloudRecord(true)` | `true` | When set to `false`, retains property in local IndexedDB but strips it from cloud commits. |
| `setSyncsToView(true)` | `false` | Emits `"didChangeSlot"` notification via `SvNotificationCenter` upon mutation. |
| `setCanEditInspection(true)` | `false` | Exposes field for direct editing in the modifier-click (Option+Click) Property Inspector. |
| `setIsSubnode(true)` | `null` | Adds slot value automatically to parent's `subnodes` array during `finalInit()`. |
| `setIsSubnodeField(true)` | `null` | Generates a navigable field tile (`SvField`) in the UI inspector hierarchy. |
| `setFinalInitProto(ClassName)` | `null` | Auto-instantiates default child objects during `finalInit()` if absent from storage. |
| `setIsBlobString(true)` | `false` | Long text slot whose payload spills to a SHA-256 text blob in storage. |
| `setIsPromiseWrapped(true)` | `false` | Auto-wraps getter return values in a Promise for async interface operations. |
| `setDuplicateOp("duplicate")` | `"nop"` | Cloning policy when duplicating nodes (`"nop"`, `"copyValue"`, `"duplicate"`). |
| `setValidValues([a, b])` | `null` | Restricts values to an allowed set, rendering dropdown options in the UI. |
| `setAllowsNullValue(true)` | `false` | Relaxes runtime validation to permit `null` slot values. |
| `setTranslationContext("ui")` | `null` | Declares i18n category for auto-translating string values. |

---

## Slot Constructor Variants

- **`newSlot(name, defaultValue)`**: Standard slot constructor with auto getter and setter.
- **`newWeakSlot(name, defaultValue)`**: Creates a slot holding a `WeakRef`. The getter unwraps the weak reference automatically; the setter wraps new values in `WeakRef`. Prevents retain cycles in parent-child back references.
- **`newSubnodeFieldSlot(name, Class)`**: Convenience constructor for navigable subnode field properties.
- **`overrideSlot(name, defaultValue)`**: Overrides a slot inherited from a superclass, preserving metadata while changing the default value.

---

## Slot Change & Getter Hooks

Auto-generated getters and setters execute optional lifecycle hooks on the owning object if defined:

```javascript
(class Character extends SvStorableNode {

    initPrototypeSlots () {
        {
            const slot = this.newSlot("inventory", null);
            slot.setSlotType("Inventory");
        }
    }

    // Optional lazy initialization hook called BEFORE getter returns value
    willGetSlotInventory () {
        if (!this._inventory) {
            this.setInventory(Inventory.clone());
        }
    }

    // Optional hook called BEFORE setter updates value
    willUpdateSlotInventory (oldVal, newVal) {
        console.log("Inventory changing from", oldVal, "to", newVal);
    }

    // Optional hook called AFTER setter updates value
    didUpdateSlotInventory (oldVal, newVal) {
        this.recalculateTotalWeight();
    }

}.initThisClass());
```

---

## Runtime Type Checking

Auto-generated setters enforce **runtime type checks** against `setSlotType()`. When a type mismatch occurs (e.g. attempting to pass a string to a `Number` slot), the setter logs a warning and attempts safe type coercion (e.g. `Number("12")`), protecting object graph state from corrupt data.

---

## Related Guides

- [Nodes](../Nodes/index.html): Core `SvNode` domain abstraction.
- [Implementation Overview](../../Implementation%20Overview/index.html): Deep dive into slot specs and class lifecycles.
- [Slot Change Hooks](../../Notifications/Slot%20Change%20Hooks/index.html): Declarative setter hooks.

<!-- Page: docs/Technical Overview -->
Source: /docs/Technical%20Overview/

# Technical Overview

High-level architecture, core design philosophy, and system-wide concepts of the Strvct framework.

## Introduction

Strvct is an open-source, local-first **Naked Objects** framework built in client-side JavaScript. Instead of requiring developers to manually author and maintain separate domain models, UI component trees, form layouts, validators, client-side state stores, persistence mappings, localization dictionaries, and AI agent tool specifications, Strvct derives the complete application interface and operational infrastructure automatically from an annotated domain model.

Applications built with Strvct operate as single-page web applications (SPAs) executing natively in the browser. The system is designed from the ground up for **local-first execution**: application state is stored locally in IndexedDB object pools, enabling instant, zero-latency user interaction and full offline functionality. When online, local object pools synchronize transparently with versioned cloud stores.

<svg viewBox="0 0 820 240" width="820" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <style>
    text { font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; fill: #111; }
    .b { font-weight: 600; }
    .dim { fill: #666; }
    .box { fill: none; stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; }
    .fill { fill: #f0ede5; stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; }
    .flow { stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; fill: none; }
    .flow-dashed { stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; fill: none; stroke-dasharray: 4 3; }
  </style>
  <defs>
    <marker id="ato" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto">
      <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="#111"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <rect class="fill" x="40" y="20" width="740" height="65"/>
  <text x="55" y="42" class="b">Annotated Domain Model (SvStorableNode Subclasses)</text>
  <text x="55" y="60" class="dim">Single source of truth declaring slots, subnodes, and metadata annotations</text>

  <line class="flow" x1="120" y1="85" x2="120" y2="125" marker-end="url(#ato)"/>
  <line class="flow" x1="310" y1="85" x2="310" y2="125" marker-end="url(#ato)"/>
  <line class="flow" x1="500" y1="85" x2="500" y2="125" marker-end="url(#ato)"/>

  <rect class="box" x="40" y="125" width="160" height="90"/>
  <text x="55" y="147" class="b">Auto-Generated UI</text>

  <rect class="box" x="230" y="125" width="160" height="90"/>

  <rect class="box" x="420" y="125" width="160" height="90"/>

  <text x="435" y="165" class="dim">Runs in Node.js with</text>
  <text x="435" y="183" class="dim">zero DOM dependencies</text>

  <rect class="box" x="610" y="125" width="170" height="90"/>
  <text x="625" y="147" class="b">Native AI Tool Surface</text>
  <text x="625" y="165" class="dim">Constant tool size:</text>
  <text x="625" y="183" class="dim">schema-fetch &amp; patch</text>
</svg>

Unlike traditional component frameworks (React, Vue, Svelte, Flutter) or compile-time code generators:
- **No Pre-Rendered View Trees:** There is no build step that compiles templates into UI components or static layouts.
- **Lazy Runtime View Derivation:** Views are instantiated lazily in response to user navigation through the object graph. Each step inspects target node slot annotations to resolve or create the appropriate `SvNodeView`.
- **Bidirectional Live Synchronization:** Active views observe model nodes through deferred, deduplicated notifications. Updates flow bidirectionally between model and view without manual binding logic.
- **Complete Decoupling:** Model objects hold zero references to UI classes or browser DOM elements. The entire domain graph runs headlessly in Node.js for testing, batch processing, or server-side workflows.

---

## The Model-First Triad

Strvct organizes applications into three distinct layers connected by an asymmetric notification architecture:

  <text x="410" y="215" text-anchor="middle" class="dim">Model is the authoritative source of truth.</text>

### Layer Responsibilities

1. **Model Layer (`SvNode` Graph):**
   - Authoritative source of truth for all domain data and business logic.
   - Composed of objects inheriting from `SvNode` (or `SvStorableNode`).
   - Declares instance properties as **slots** enriched with metadata annotations.
   - Emits change notifications when slots or subnode arrays mutate, but holds no references to views or persistence handlers.

2. **UI Layer (`SvNodeView` Tree):**
   - Renders visual presentation using lazy, auto-generated master-detail Miller column containers (`SvStackView`, `SvNavView`, `SvTilesView`, `SvTile`).
   - Observes model notifications and pulls updated values on model mutation.
   - Sends user edit commands back to the model via standard slot setters.

3. **Storage Layer (`SvPersistentObjectPool`):**
   - Monitors model mutation notifications automatically.
   - Batches dirty objects at the end of each browser event loop into transactional IndexedDB operations.
   - Syncs versioned delta commits with cloud storage for cross-device availability.

---

## The Multi-Reader Annotation Bridge

The cornerstone of Strvct's architecture is the **Slot Annotation System**. Instead of raw instance variables, domain properties are declared as slots with metadata annotations.

Slot annotations act as a **multi-reader decoupling bridge**. Each framework subsystem reads slot metadata independently to perform its job without cross-system dependencies:

```
                          +---> UI Generation (Property Tiles & Control Types)
                          |
                          +---> Local Storage & Cloud Sync (IndexedDB Records)
                          |
[ Slot Metadata Bridge ] -+---> Notification Engine (Coalesced Sync Passes)
                          |
                          +---> Native AI Tool Surface (JSON Patch Validation)
                          |
                          +---> Accessibility & i18n (ARIA Roles & Translation)
```

| Annotation Settor | Purpose & Subsystem Consumer |
|---|---|
| `setSlotType("String")` | Selects tile UI input control type, runtime type validation, and AI JSON schema generation. |
| `setShouldStoreSlot(true)` | Directs `SvPersistentObjectPool` to include property in serialized storage records. |
| `setSyncsToView(true)` | Instructs model setter to post notification triggers to active observing views. |
| `setCanEditInspection(true)` | Exposes property in the modifier-click (Option+Click) live Property Inspector. |
| `setIsSubnodeField(true)` | Exposes complex properties as navigable child nodes in the UI inspector hierarchy. |
| `setFinalInitProto(ClassName)` | Auto-instantiates default child objects during initialization if absent from storage. |

---

## UI Synchronization Engine

Strvct enforces an asymmetric, notification-driven synchronization architecture:

1. **Push Phase (User Action):** When a user edits a property in the UI, the view calls the corresponding setter on the model node (e.g., `character.setName("Thorin")`).
2. **Notification Phase:** The generated slot setter verifies the type, updates internal state, and posts a named change notification via `SvNotificationCenter`.
3. **Pull Phase (Deferred View Sync):** Observing views receive the notification and schedule a sync pass with `SvSyncScheduler`.
4. **Coalescing & Loop Avoidance:** `SvSyncScheduler` deduplicates multiple mutations within the same event loop, executing a single UI re-render pass at the end of the loop. If setter values have converged, sync halts automatically, preventing infinite update loops.
5. **Memory Safety:** Notifications use weak-reference observation patterns, allowing unreferenced views and models to be garbage-collected cleanly without manual listener detachment.

---

## Local & Cloud Persistence

Strvct combines local-first speed with seamless cloud synchronization:

### 1. Local Object Pools (IndexedDB)
- Application data is divided into **Object Pools** (one pool per document/aggregate root).
- Each domain object is stored as a JSON row keyed by `poolId` and `puuid` (persistent UUID).
- Object references within a pool are stored as `{ "*": puuid }`.
- External cross-pool references are stored as `{ "**": poolId }`.
- Mutations queue objects automatically for end-of-event-loop atomic IndexedDB commits.

### 2. SHA-256 Content-Addressable Blob Store
- Large binary assets (images, audio, files) are stored separately in `SvBlobPool`.
- Keys are computed as SHA-256 content hashes, providing automatic binary deduplication.
- Records store hash references rather than raw binary data, keeping IndexedDB records lean and fast.

### 3. Versioned Cloud Commits
- Cloud persistence mirror the same row format as local IndexedDB.
- Saving a document computes delta rows modified since the last acknowledged pool version and posts an atomic commit.
- Conflicts are detected deterministically per pool version rather than silently overwriting data.

---

## Content-Addressable Resource Delivery (CAM)

Real-world Naked Objects applications load hundreds of domain classes, view handlers, and style assets into the browser. Traditional ES module loading (hundreds of individual HTTP requests) creates severe network latency, while standard Webpack/Vite bundlers invalidate full chunks on minor file edits.

Strvct solves this with a **Content-Addressable Memory (CAM)** build and delivery pipeline:

```
[ Build Stage: ImportsIndexer ]
  Scan _imports.json tree ---> Compute SHA-256 for each file
  ---> Produce _index.json (path -> hash) & _cam.json.zip (compressed content)

[ Runtime Stage: SvResourceManager & SvHashCache ]
  Fetch _index.json ---> Compare against IndexedDB SvHashCache
  ---> If delta ratio > 30%: Download _cam.json.zip in 1 request
  ---> If delta ratio <= 30%: Download only missing hash files
```

### Key Benefits of CAM Delivery:
- **Hash-Based Caching:** Assets are addressed and cached in IndexedDB by SHA-256 hash rather than URL path.
- **Zero-Churn Redeployment:** Modifying a single source file invalidates only that file's hash in the cache; returning users download only the edited file.
- **Cross-App Shared Caching:** Multiple Strvct applications running on the same origin share the local hash cache for common framework classes.
- **Full Debugger Support:** JavaScript source files are evaluated dynamically via `eval()` with embedded `sourceURL` annotations, providing complete DevTools debugger capabilities (breakpoints, stack traces, step execution).

---

## Architectural Capabilities ("For Free")

Because Strvct centralizes the pipeline from slot annotations to runtime views, several high-value capabilities fall out of the architecture automatically:

1. **Natively AI-Operable Model:** Every class exposes a constant-size tool surface (`schema-fetch` + `apply-patch`). AI agents inspect schemas and patch live object graphs directly with automatic schema validation.
2. **Headless Execution:** Domain models contain zero DOM dependencies and execute natively under Node.js for ultra-fast unit testing, simulations, or server execution.
3. **Automatic Mobile Responsiveness:** Navigation columns (`SvStackView`) automatically collapse into mobile push/pop stacks with interactive breadcrumb headers on narrow viewports.
4. **Live Property Inspector:** Modifier-clicking (Option+Click) any tile reveals a live inspector displaying all declared slots, storage flags, and validation states.
5. **Type-Safe Cross-Window Drag & Drop:** Tiles support serialization to JSON MIME types for dragging data across browser windows, desktop apps, or Strvct instances.
6. **Universal Accessibility & Localization:** ARIA roles, keyboard navigation, focus management, and AI string translation are applied centrally at the tile primitive level.

---

# Views

The view layer: auto-generated UI, custom views, and programmatic styling.

The entire view system is built from a small number of composable elements: a node, a tile, a column, and a master-detail split. These four pieces nest recursively — a column of tiles where selecting a tile opens another column — so the same structure that displays a flat list also handles arbitrarily deep, mixed-orientation navigation without any additional wiring.

The view hierarchy wraps DOM elements rather than extending them. This is deliberate: the DOM API is large and mutable, and subclassing it tightly couples framework code to browser internals that change across engines and versions. Wrapping keeps the boundary clean — each layer in the class chain adds exactly one capability (visibility, event listening, gestures, layout, styling), so any layer can be understood, tested, or replaced independently.

  
    text { font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; fill: #111; }
    .b { font-weight: 600; }
    .dim { fill: #666; }
    .box { fill: none; stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; }
    .fill { fill: #f0ede5; stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; }
    .flow { stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; fill: none; }
  
  
    
      
    
  
  
  SvNode
  model node with slots, subnodes, annotations
  - 
  
  Tile
  renders one node; shows title, subtitle, optional inline
  editor, selection state, accessibility metadata
  - 
  
  Column / Stack
  ordered list of tiles for a node's subnodes,
  vertical or horizontal per node preference
  - 
  
  Master-Detail Split
  column on one side, detail view on the other;
  selecting a tile opens its node as the next column,
  composing recursively (Miller-columns-style)
  Tiles, columns, and splits nest recursively, so a single composition handles arbitrary navigation depth and mixed orientations.

- Auto-Generated Views
- Custom Views
- Companion View
- Programmatic Styling
- Themes and Style States
- Responsive

# Auto-Generated Views

How the view layer connects to model nodes, resolves view classes, synchronizes state, and provides navigation without hand-authored UI code.

## Overview

In STRVCT, every domain node (`SvNode`) automatically receives a visual presentation: the framework discovers the matching view class, instantiates views lazily on demand, wires up observation notifications, and keeps views synchronized as model slots mutate.

---

## `SvDomView` Single-Inheritance Layering

Rather than subclassing raw HTML elements directly, STRVCT wraps DOM elements in a single-inheritance hierarchy where each layer adds one capability:

| View Class Layer | Added Capability |
|---|---|
| **`SvElementDomView`** | Wraps DOM element; manages creation, type, and class attributes. |
| **`SvVisibleDomView`** | Visibility toggling (`setIsVisible(bool)`). |
| **`SvResponderDomView`** | Responder chain for keyboard and mouse event routing. |
| **`SvListenerDomView`** | DOM event listener registration and removal. |
| **`SvControlDomView`** | Target/action pattern connecting views to event handlers. |
| **`SvSelectableDomView`** | Selection state with styled visual feedback. |
| **`SvEditableDomView`** | Content editability and edit mode toggling. |
| **`SvGesturableDomView`** | Gesture recognizers (tap, double-tap, pan, long-press, pinch). |
| **`SvFlexDomView`** | Flexbox layout properties (direction, wrap, grow, shrink, alignment). |
| **`SvStyledDomView`** | State-based styling (unselected, selected, active, disabled) with theme support. |
| **`SvSubviewsDomView`** | Parent/child subview hierarchy management. |
| **`SvCssDomView`** | Applies CSS variables from dictionaries to element styles. |
| **`SvDomView`** | Aggregates all layers above into the complete DOM view wrapper. |
| **`SvNodeView`** | Binds model `SvNode` to DOM presentation; handles observation & sync. |

---

## `SvNodeView` Bridge Methods

`SvNodeView` is the primary class for application views:
- `setNode(aNode)`: Assigns a model node and registers change observations via `SvNotificationCenter`.
- `syncFromNode()`: Diffs visible subnodes against active subviews, instantiating, reusing, or purging views as needed.
- `subviewProtoForSubnode(aSubnode)`: Resolves which view class to instantiate for a child subnode.
- `syncCssFromNode()`: Applies CSS variables defined on the model node to the DOM element.

---

## View Resolution Lookup Algorithm

When a node becomes visible, the framework discovers its view class using naming conventions:

1. **Explicit Override:** Check for an explicit `nodeViewClassName` override on the node.
2. **Inheritance Walk:** Walk the node's class hierarchy from most-derived to base (`SvNode`).
3. **Convention Lookup:** For each class ancestor, check for `ClassName + "View"` in global scope.
4. **Fallback:** If no match is found down to the root, fall back to default `SvNodeView`.

*Example:* For `Character` extending `SvStorableNode`, resolution checks `CharacterView` $\rightarrow$ `SvStorableNodeView` $\rightarrow$ `SvNodeView`.

---

## Navigation Containers (`SvStackView` & `SvBrowserView`)

### `SvStackView`
`SvStackView` is the recursive building block of navigation, splitting into two areas:
- **`SvNavView` (Master):** A column containing a header, scrollable `SvTilesView`, and footer.
- **`otherView` (Detail):** Content area for the selected tile—typically a child `SvStackView`.

Selecting a tile creates a new child `SvStackView` in the detail area. **Orientation** is set per node (`"right"` for horizontal master-left/detail-right, `"down"` for vertical master-top/detail-below).

### `SvBrowserView`
Top-level application container managing nested `SvStackView` columns to arbitrary depth. Includes a breadcrumb header that auto-compacts on narrow viewports:
- `navigateToNode(aNode)`: Navigates directly to a target node in the graph.
- `selectNodePathArray(pathArray)`: Programmatically sets the full navigation path.

---

## Tile Classes & Field Tiles

Tiles are individual items rendered inside `SvTilesView` columns:

| Tile Class | Purpose & Visual Presentation |
|---|---|
| **`SvTile`** | Base tile class. Handles selection, long-press reorder, slide-to-delete, and style state cascades. |
| **`SvTitledTile`** | Default tile. Displays title, subtitle, and note from `SvSummaryNode`. |
| **`SvHeaderTile`** | Non-selectable section header tile. |
| **`SvBreadCrumbsTile`** | Compact breadcrumb trail tile. |

### Field Tiles (`SvFieldTile`):

Field tiles render key-value property slots as editable controls:

| Field Tile Class | Property Control Type |
|---|---|
| **`SvStringFieldTile`** | Single-line text input |
| **`SvTextAreaFieldTile`** | Multi-line text area editor |
| **`SvBooleanFieldTile`** | Checkbox toggle control |
| **`SvPasswordFieldTile`** | Masked password text input |
| **`SvActionFieldTile`** | Button triggering a node method |
| **`SvPointerFieldTile`** | Object reference with navigation arrow |
| **`SvImageWellFieldTile`** | Image preview well with drag-and-drop support |
| **`SvVideoWellFieldTile`** | Video player well with drag-and-drop support |

---

# Companion View

A persistent secondary context docked alongside a node's navigation, collapsing behind an edge handle or disappearing as the viewport narrows.

## Overview

A **companion** is a secondary region the view layer displays alongside a node's primary master-detail navigation: a chat panel beside a gaming session, a property inspector beside a document editor, or a reference pane beside a campaign tree.

Unlike popovers or modal drawers, a docked companion lives in normal layout flow: it reserves real layout space, causing adjacent navigation columns to compact smoothly without obscuring content.

<svg viewBox="0 0 820 280" width="820" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <style>
    text { font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; fill: #111; }
    .b { font-weight: 600; }
    .dim { fill: #666; }
    .box { fill: none; stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; }
    .fill { fill: #f0ede5; stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; }
    .flow { stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; fill: none; }
  </style>
  <defs>
    <marker id="acm" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto">
      <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="#111"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <rect class="box" x="25" y="20" width="770" height="240"/>
  <text x="40" y="42" class="b">SvStackView / SvDetailView Layout Container</text>

---

## Model-View Boundary Protocol (`nodeCompanionNode`)

A domain node opts into displaying a companion by answering the optional protocol method:

```javascript
nodeCompanionNode () {
    return this.someOwnedCompanionNode(); // returns the companion root node, or null for none
}
```

The node specifies *which* node to show alongside itself, but zero UI details: width, axis, pinning, and collapse state are managed entirely by the view layer. This maintains strict headless testability.

---

## The Three Display States

| State | Visual Behavior | Space Allocation |
|---|---|---|
| **`docked`** | Panel is expanded alongside or beneath navigation columns. | Reserves full length (`companionReservedWidth()`); columns compact to fit. |
| **`tab`** | Panel is collapsed into a zero-width tab handle. | Panel occupies 0px. Adjacent `SvNavView` displays expansion handle. |
| **`hidden`** | Panel and handle are both suppressed. | Viewport is too narrow to offer companion without breaking primary content. |

---

## Space Arbitration & Keyboard Shortcuts

`SvDetailView` arbitrates layout space using `setAvailableLength()`:

- **Threshold Check:** If available width falls below `tabLength`, mode switches to `hidden`.
- **User Pinning:** Clicking the edge handle toggles between `docked` and `tab`, persisting the choice as `userMode`.
- **Shortcut:** Pressing **Meta+\\** (Cmd+\\ or Ctrl+\\) toggles the deepest visible companion in the active navigation chain.

---

## View Class Structure

```
SvStackView
 └─ SvDetailView                       (owns space arbitration)
     ├── childStackView                (primary flexible navigation)
     └── SvCompanionView              (node = nodeCompanionNode())
         ├── contentView              (embedded isolated SvBrowserView)
         ├── SvEdgeHandleView         (collapse/expand handle)
         └── SvCompanionTabView       (internal badge plumbing)
```

---

## Theming & CSS Variables

| CSS Variable | Applies To |
|---|---|
| `--SvCompanion-bg` | Companion panel background color |
| `--SvCompanionTab-color` | Legacy tab text styling |
| `--SvCompanionTab-border-color` | Legacy tab border color |

<!-- Page: docs/Views/Custom Views -->
Source: /docs/Views/Custom%20Views/

# Custom Views

Authoring custom view classes, DOM wrappers, flex shortcuts, and model synchronization for specialized media.

## Overview

While auto-generated views handle structured domain data, custom view classes are created for **specialized media** where spatial layout carries irreducible domain meaning: WebGL 3D viewports, canvas drawing, media players, overlay panels, or battle maps.

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                         Custom View Lifecycle                           |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  1. Extend SvNodeView  -->  2. Instantiate via clone()  --> 3. addSubview |
|  4. Chained Setters    -->  5. syncFromNode()           --> 6. DevTools  |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

---

## The Custom View Pattern

Custom views extend `SvDomView` (or `SvNodeView`) and perform setup inside `init()`:

```javascript
(class MyOverlayView extends SvNodeView {

    init () {
        super.init();
        this.setPosition("fixed");
        this.setTop("0");
        this.setLeft("0");
        this.setWidth("100vw");
        this.setHeight("100vh");
        this.makeFlexAndCenterContent();
        this.setBackgroundColor("rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)");
        this.setZIndex(9999);

        // Create child view via clone()
        this._label = SvDomView.clone();
        this._label.setColor("white");
        this._label.setFontSize("24px");
        this.addSubview(this._label);

        return this;
    }

    syncFromNode () {
        super.syncFromNode();
        const node = this.node();
        if (node) {
            this._label.setInnerHTML(node.statusText());
        }
    }

}.initThisClass());
```

---

## View Construction Rules: `clone()` vs `new`

- **Always Use `clone()`:** View instances MUST be instantiated via `Class.clone()` rather than `new Class()`.
- **Initialization Phases:** `clone()` executes the three-phase lifecycle automatically: `init()` $\rightarrow$ `finalInit()` $\rightarrow$ `afterInit()`.
- **View Tree & DOM Tree:** `this.addSubview(childView)` establishes both the internal framework subview hierarchy and appends the underlying DOM element.

---

## `SvFlexDomView` Layout Shortcuts

| Shortcut Method | CSS Property Modifications |
|---|---|
| `makeFlexAndCenterContent()` | Sets `display: flex`, `justify-content: center`, `align-items: center`. |
| `makeStandardFlexView()` | Sets `display: flex`, `position: relative`, `overflow: hidden`. |
| `fillParentView()` | Sets `width: 100%` and `height: 100%`. |
| `newFlexSubview()` | Creates and appends a flex child with `min-width: 0` and `min-height: 0`. |

---

## Related Guides

- [Auto-Generated Views](../Auto-Generated%20Views/index.html): View resolution and stack containers.
- [Responsive Views](../Responsive/index.html): Viewport compaction and column collapse.

<!-- Page: docs/Views/Programmatic Styling -->
Source: /docs/Views/Programmatic%20Styling/

# Programmatic Styling

Named CSS methods, the chainable API, and why STRVCT avoids CSS files.

## Why No CSS Files?

### The cascade is additive

The CSS cascade is designed for documents: you declare rules, the browser resolves conflicts by specificity and source order, and the result is static. You can mutate individual rules through the CSSOM, but the cascade itself is additive — removing a rule doesn't restore a known-good state, it just lets some other rule win, potentially one you didn't intend. This makes the cascade unreliable for UI components whose appearance changes frequently at runtime.

### State combinatorics

The deeper problem is combinatorial. Consider the independent states a single view might have: editable or read-only, selected or unselected, highlighted or not, showing an error, previously navigated, disabled. Five boolean states produce 32 combinations, and each combination may need distinct styling. In a stylesheet, each combination requires its own selector or class chain — and the count doubles with every new state. You can try to treat each state independently (`.selected` sets some properties, `.error` sets others), but that only works when the states don't interact visually. When "selected + error" needs to look different from the sum of "selected" and "error" applied separately, you're back to enumerating combinations.

### Theming compounds the problem

CSS custom properties can swap values at runtime, but they don't help with the structural problem of *which properties to set in which state combinations*. When a user customizes a theme, or different regions of the UI use different themes simultaneously, every state combination now has a theme axis too. The custom properties handle the value lookup, but the combinatorial selector structure they plug into still has to be authored and maintained by hand.

### The programmatic alternative

Programmatic styling sidesteps all of this. Each state applies its visual changes directly to the element, and the results compose naturally — enabling "selected" and "error" at the same time just means both sets of property changes are applied, with explicit logic for cases where they interact. Themes are dictionaries of values that can be swapped or scoped to any subtree at any time — no cascade resolution, just direct assignment. The styling logic lives alongside the view logic that drives it, so the two can't drift apart.

## Named Property Methods

Every view inherits named setter/getter pairs for standard CSS properties. These are the primary styling API:

```javascript
this.setBackgroundColor("rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)");
this.setPosition("fixed");
this.setDisplay("flex");
this.setZIndex(9999);
this.setTop("0");
this.setLeft("0");
this.setWidth("100vw");
this.setHeight("100vh");
this.setFontSize("14px");
this.setColor("white");
this.setBorderRadius("8px");
this.setOverflow("hidden");
this.setPadding("16px");
this.setBoxShadow("0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)");
```

Every setter returns `this`, so calls chain naturally. Each property also has a corresponding getter (e.g. `backgroundColor()`, `fontSize()`).

## Flexbox Methods

`SvFlexDomView` adds named methods for every flexbox property:

```javascript
this.setDisplay("flex");
this.setFlexDirection("column");
this.setJustifyContent("center");
this.setAlignItems("stretch");
this.setFlexWrap("wrap");
this.setFlexGrow(1);
this.setFlexShrink(0);
this.setFlexBasis("auto");
this.setGap("8px");
```

## Layout Convenience Methods

`SvFlexDomView` also provides higher-level shortcuts for common multi-property patterns:

| Method | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| `makeFlexAndCenterContent()` | Sets display flex, centers both axes |
| `flexCenterContent()` | Centers content horizontally and vertically |
| `makeStandardFlexView()` | Flex display, relative positioning, centered, overflow hidden |
| `fillParentView()` | Sets width and height to 100% |
| `newFlexSubview()` | Creates and adds a flex child with min dimensions set |

## Sizing Shortcuts

Convenience methods for constrained sizing:

| Method | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| `setMinAndMaxWidth(v)` | Sets min-width, max-width, and width to the same value |
| `setMinAndMaxHeight(v)` | Sets min-height, max-height, and height to the same value |
| `setMinAndMaxWidthAndHeight(v)` | Sets all six sizing properties at once |

These are useful for fixed-size elements like icons or thumbnails where you want all constraints to agree.

## Node-Driven CSS

Nodes can also request CSS properties that get applied to their view automatically. A node implements `cssVariableDict()` to return a dictionary of CSS key/value pairs:

```javascript
cssVariableDict () {
    return {
        "color": this.isActive() ? "white" : "gray",
        "--accent-color": this.themeColor()
    };
}
```

During the normal sync cycle, `SvNodeView.syncCssFromNode()` picks up this dictionary and applies it to the view's DOM element. This lets model logic influence presentation without the node needing any reference to its view — the node declares what it wants, and the view system handles the rest.

In general, prefer keeping styling in the view layer. Node-driven CSS is available for cases where the model genuinely determines a visual property (e.g. a user-chosen color or a status-dependent highlight), but most styling belongs in views or themes, not in model code.

## Low-Level Access

For unusual CSS properties that don't have a named method, `SvCssDomView` provides generic accessors:

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `setCssProperty(key, value)` | Sets any CSS property by name |
| `getCssProperty(key)` | Gets the computed value |
| `removeCssProperty(key)` | Removes a property |

These should be rare in practice — the named methods cover the vast majority of styling needs.


---

<!-- Page: docs/Views/Responsive -->
Source: /docs/Views/Responsive/

# Responsive Views

Automatic viewport compaction, last-column stretching, and per-node width hooks without per-screen layout code.

## Overview

Responsive behavior in STRVCT is not a separate rendering mode or set of CSS breakpoints. The same master-detail composition that produces a multi-column Miller view on a wide desktop produces a one-column stack with breadcrumbs on a phone, because `SvStackView` measures available width and automatically collapses columns that would overflow the viewport.

This behavior—**automatic collapsing**—falls out of the same primitives used for navigation at any width; there is zero separate "mobile" code path in the view hierarchy.

<svg viewBox="0 0 820 320" width="820" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <style>
    text { font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; fill: #111; }
    .b { font-weight: 600; }
    .dim { fill: #666; }
    .box { fill: none; stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; }
    .fill { fill: #f0ede5; stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; }
    .flow { stroke: #111; stroke-width: 1; fill: none; }
  </style>
  <defs>
    <marker id="are" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto">
      <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="#111"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <!-- Desktop Wide Viewport (Left) -->
  <rect class="box" x="25" y="20" width="360" height="240"/>
  <text x="40" y="42" class="b">Wide Desktop Viewport (&gt; 800px)</text>

  <rect class="fill" x="40" y="60" width="100" height="180"/>
  <text x="48" y="80" class="b">Column 1</text>
  <text x="48" y="98" class="dim">Expanded</text>

  <rect class="fill" x="150" y="60" width="100" height="180"/>
  <text x="158" y="80" class="b">Column 2</text>
  <text x="158" y="98" class="dim">Expanded</text>

  <rect class="fill" x="260" y="60" width="110" height="180"/>
  <text x="268" y="80" class="b">Column 3</text>
  <text x="268" y="98" class="dim">Expanded</text>

  <!-- Transition Arrow -->
  <line class="flow" x1="395" y1="140" x2="425" y2="140" marker-end="url(#are)"/>

  <!-- Mobile Narrow Viewport (Right) -->
  <rect class="box" x="435" y="20" width="360" height="240"/>
  <text x="450" y="42" class="b">Narrow Mobile Viewport (&lt; 480px)</text>

  <rect class="fill" x="450" y="60" width="330" height="30"/>
  <text x="465" y="80" class="b">Breadcrumbs: Workspace &gt; Projects</text>

  <rect class="fill" x="450" y="100" width="330" height="140"/>
  <text x="465" y="120" class="b">Column 3 (Active Column - 100% Width)</text>
  <text x="465" y="140" class="dim">Columns 1 &amp; 2 auto-collapsed (display: none)</text>
</svg>

---

## The Two Layout Mechanisms

### 1. Compaction (`compactNavAsNeeded`)
`SvStackView.compactNavAsNeeded()` walks the stack chain from outermost (leftmost) to innermost (rightmost), summing target widths against available viewport space (`topViewWidth()`):
- **Fits:** The column is `uncollapse()`d and displayed.
- **Overflows:** Earlier columns are `collapse()`d (`display: none`). The current (deepest) column stays visible as long as possible.

### 2. Last-Column Stretch (`updateWidthForWindow`)
`SvNavView.updateWidthForWindow()` determines width for visible columns:
- If `targetWidth() >= windowWidth`, the column takes `width: 100%`.
- If a column is the last visible column AND `windowWidth < targetWidth * 2`, it stretches to `width: 100%` to fill available slack instead of leaving dead space.

---

## Per-Node Layout Protocol Hooks

Domain nodes can influence layout without writing custom view code:

| Node Method | Purpose & Behavior |
|---|---|
| `nodeMinTileWidth()` | Declares a minimum tile width floor for the column. Useful for wide property inspectors. |
| `nodeFillsRemainingWidth()` | When `true`, forces the column to stretch to 100% width whenever it is the last visible column. Useful for document editors or chat logs. |

---

## Viewport vs Device Detection

- **`SvWebBrowserWindow.shared().width()`**: Returns current viewport width in CSS pixels. Always use this for layout and compaction decisions.
- **`SvWebBrowserWindow.shared().isOnMobile()`**: User-agent string match (iPhone/Android). Use *only* for touch-gesture or platform-specific permissions, never for column width sizing.

---

## iOS Safari Visual Viewport Note

On iPhone Safari, CSS `100vh` units fail to subtract the animated URL bar area (~40px overflow). The reliable fix is binding root page height to `window.visualViewport.height` during `visualViewport.resize` and `orientationchange` events.

---

- [Auto-Generated Views](../Auto-Generated%20Views/index.html): Navigation containers and tiles.
- [Companion View](../Companion%20View/index.html): Space arbitration for docked companions.
